#1750. Longo: Rabiot renewal, Endrick, Inacio and more – key topics during Friday’s summit

Gerry Cardinale had a meeting with the AC Milan management at Casa Milan yesterday, during which there were four key topics, according to reports.

Cardinale has arrived in the city in good time for Milan’s game against Frosinone tomorrow. Yesterday, there was a summit with the Milan management, including the CEO Massimo Calvelli, Head of Football Intelligence Bobby Gardiner, and Head of Recruitment Tiago Estevão.

This was reported by Sky Italia (via MilanEye) and various outlets, highlighting how Cardinale wants to be ready for the January window and even the summer window. Markus Krösche will be there to help him with that, set to be announced next week, as Gazzetta dello Sport reported.

According to Daniele Longo, there were four key topics during the meeting: the renewal of Adrien Rabiot (which is close), the Endrick pursuit (which is heating up), Goncalo Inacio for the defence, and Krösche’s announcement.

There could be a lot of big movement in the coming months, in other words, as Cardinale is really pushing for these things to materialise. Of course, other matters were also discussed during the meeting but as Longo highlighted, those mentioned above were the main ones.

Cardinale will be at Milanello today and then he will also be in the stands for the game tomorrow, showing his support for the team yet again.

#1749. Arsenal face fresh £80m transfer threat as PSG consider January response to Desire Doue injury

By Naim Beneddra | 22 Nov 2026 12:11

Arsenal could face a fresh complication in their pursuit of Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi, with Paris Saint-Germain reportedly considering whether to accelerate their interest in the Frenchman following Desire Doue's serious knee injury.

The European champions were already among the clubs monitoring Kroupi ahead of the January transfer window, but their attacking situation has become considerably more difficult after Doue was stretchered off during Saturday's 3-2 Ligue 1 victory over Nice. PSG confirmed on Sunday that the 21-year-old has ruptured the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee and will undergo surgery before the end of November.

According to TEAMtalk transfer correspondent Graeme Bailey, PSG hold a strong interest in the Bournemouth attacker, who is also wanted by Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur. The French champions could now consider stepping up their pursuit, although no formal approach or offer has been reported.

Any attempt to secure the youngster's signature would present a substantial financial challenge. Bournemouth are understood to value Kroupi at upwards of £80m and have shown little willingness to entertain a mid-season departure, despite increasing attention from some of Europe's leading clubs.

Doue's confirmed ACL rupture has left Luis Enrique facing a potentially season-ending absence in a forward line already weakened by the loss of Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

The France international had scored PSG's second goal against Nice before suffering the injury late in the first half. He required treatment on the pitch and was eventually carried off on a stretcher, with Ferran Torres replacing him and subsequently scoring the winning goal.

Luis Enrique warned after the match that the injury was serious, although he stressed that further medical examinations were needed to establish its precise nature.

Those concerns were confirmed on Sunday when PSG announced that Doue had suffered a rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee. The club also confirmed that the forward would undergo surgery before the end of November.

Although PSG have not announced a definitive recovery timetable, the severity of the injury raises serious doubts about whether Doue will play again this season.

The setback follows Kvaratskhelia's ACL injury during PSG's Champions League victory over Barcelona in October, which has already deprived Enrique of another important attacking option.

Paris still possess considerable depth, with Ousmane Dembele, Torres, Manuel Akliouche and Mika Godts among the players available to the Spanish coach. Nevertheless, losing two influential attackers in relatively quick succession could alter the club's approach to the January window.

That is where Kroupi's situation becomes particularly interesting.

Bailey reports that PSG are admirers of the Bournemouth forward and that Doue's injury could encourage them to intensify an interest that existed well before Saturday's events.

Kroupi would not necessarily represent a direct replacement for Doue. Although capable of operating across the attacking line, he is primarily a centre-forward, meaning any move would also reflect a broader decision about how Enrique wishes to reshape his available options.

There is currently no indication that PSG have opened negotiations with Bournemouth or made Kroupi their preferred January target. The possibility of an accelerated approach remains dependent on the club's assessment of its attacking needs.

For Arsenal, the prospect of renewed PSG interest adds another dimension to an already complicated transfer pursuit.

The Gunners have been following Kroupi's development for several months, while Tottenham have also been linked with the attacker. Barcelona and Bayern Munich are among the other European clubs reportedly keeping a close eye on his progress.

Kroupi's emergence has made him one of Bournemouth's most valuable assets. The former Lorient forward scored 13 Premier League goals last season and has since earned international recognition with France, strengthening his reputation as one of the country's most promising young attacking talents.

However, Bournemouth are under little pressure to sanction an immediate sale. Kroupi remains under contract until June 2030, and the Cherries are determined to benefit from his performances during the remainder of the campaign.

David Ornstein recently indicated in The Athletic that a January transfer was unlikely, with Bournemouth expected to be more receptive to offers next summer. The journalist also suggested that the player could favour a move abroad when the time comes to leave the Vitality Stadium.

That possibility represents a further concern for Arsenal, particularly given PSG's existing interest and Kroupi's connections with French football.

The financial demands are equally significant. Bournemouth have been linked with an asking price of at least £80m, although other reports have suggested that an even larger offer could be required to secure an agreement.

Those figures reflect the club's negotiating position rather than a confirmed bid from any interested party.

Arsenal's previously reported difficulties in securing a January deal therefore remain relevant regardless of whether PSG decide to make their interest more concrete.

A significant offer from Paris could potentially change the competitive landscape, particularly if the French champions decide that their injury problems justify an expensive winter investment.

Yet Bournemouth's position is unlikely to soften simply because another club has suffered an attacking setback. Any January approach would have to overcome the same contractual and financial obstacles facing Arsenal and Tottenham.

For now, PSG's growing need for attacking cover provides a new consideration in Kroupi's future, but the immediate question for all three interested clubs is whether Bournemouth can be persuaded to discuss a transfer before the summer.

#1748. Manchester United XI vs Sporting: Confirmed team news, predicted lineup and injury latest for Champions League

The Argentine endured a horror start to his tenure at Old Trafford with a heavy 4-0 defeat by Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

The Red Devils were down to ten men inside eight minutes when Leny Yoro was sent off for denying Alexander Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity.

United suffered no injury blows on Merseyside, but the result was “painful” according to their new head coach, and he will be looking to put things right immediately in Europe’s top competition on Wednesday.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss sprung a surprise with his inclusion of Matthijs de Ligt in his starting XI at Anfield, with the Dutchman having been sidelined for over a year with a persistent back injury.

The centre-half looked awkward for much of the match, and his selection was scrutinised intensely afterwards.

It remains to be seen whether he will play again here, with Harry Maguire introduced in the first half and shoring up United’s back five.

The England international should start here, perhaps alongisde Yoro, who will not be suspended for this match with his ban only for league games.

That could see Lisandro Martinez plugged at left-back once more, although the Argentine had to shift back inside after Yoro’s red card, with Dorgu shifting back to wing-back from his left wing berth.

Diogo Dalot failed to truly impress on Merseyside and could see himself rotated for Noussair Mazraoui, while in the engine room, Youri Tielemans was hooked for Mason Mount in the second half.

Bryan Mbeumo was the man sacrificed following the sending-off as Pochettino resorted to damage limitation, but the Cameroon international should get the nod here.

#1747. Prediction: Feyenoord vs Porto

Feyenoord and Porto meet at De Kuip on Tuesday night with both clubs under pressure to revive their Champions League campaigns.

Having collected just three points from their opening four league-phase matches, the Dutch side sit 32nd in the 36-team table, while Porto are only slightly better off in 26th place. With the knockout rounds already beginning to drift out of sight for both teams, victory could prove pivotal.

Feyenoord head into the contest in poor form and desperately searching for a positive result after six matches without a win in all competitions.

Their latest setback came at the weekend when they were beaten 3-2 at home by Excelsior, a result made all the more painful by the fact it marked Excelsior’s first league victory at De Kuip in 46 years. Giovanni van Bronckhorst’s side began brightly through an early goal from Givairo Read, but three unanswered goals left Jan Plug’s late strike as little more than a consolation.

The defeat followed a 5-3 loss away to Heerenveen and a 3-0 home defeat to Inter Milan in the Champions League, meaning Feyenoord have conceded at least three goals in each of their last three matches.

Defensive concerns have become a major issue. The Dutch club have now lost 10 of their last 13 European fixtures and have conceded the opening goal in each of their last seven Champions League outings. That sequence includes defeats against Barcelona, Real Betis and Inter Milan, with their only victory in the current campaign coming against Como.

With memories of last season’s disappointing Europa League campaign, when they finished 29th in the league phase, another defeat would leave their hopes of reaching the knockout stages hanging by a thread.

Anis Hadj Moussa is being assessed after returning from international duty with an ankle injury that forced him to miss the defeat against Excelsior.

Tsuyoshi Watanabe is also a doubt after being substituted at half-time on Saturday with a foot problem.

Jakub Moder and Bart Nieuwkoop remain unavailable through injury, while Thomas Beelen, Jordan Bos and Jerry St. Juste are all expected to miss out as well, leaving Van Bronckhorst short of defensive options.

Former Arsenal winger Reiss Nelson made his first start for the club at the weekend, but Luciano Valente could be recalled on the left flank for Tuesday’s encounter.

Porto arrive in Rotterdam with considerably more momentum despite their difficult start to the Champions League campaign.

Francesco Farioli’s side finally claimed their first victory of the league phase on matchday four, producing an emphatic 4-1 win over Napoli. Jan Bednarek, Gabri Veiga, Jakub Kiwior and Samu Omorodion all found the net as the Portuguese side responded impressively after losing their opening three European matches against Manchester City, Real Betis and PSV Eindhoven.

Domestic form has been excellent. Porto have won all 11 of their Primeira Liga matches and already hold a five-point lead at the top of the table. Their most recent outing was less straightforward, though, as they required a penalty shootout to overcome third-tier Paredes in the Taca de Portugal after a 1-1 draw across 120 minutes, due to an extremely unusual own-goal.

The Dragons are competing in the Champions League main stage for the first time in three years and are hoping to reach the knockout rounds for the third consecutive appearance.

However, their record in the Netherlands offers some encouragement for Feyenoord. Porto have failed to win any of their past four away matches against Dutch opponents, drawing two and losing two. Their previous visits to De Kuip ended in a draw in 1993 and a 2-0 defeat in 2019.

Vasco Sousa remains sidelined with a long-term leg injury. Former Manchester United defender Chris Smalling is struggling with a knee issue and is also ineligible, having not been included in Porto’s Champions League squad.

William Gomes has returned to training after recovering from an ankle problem, but his involvement remains uncertain.

Midfielder In-beom Hwang is set for an emotional return against his former club after joining Porto from Feyenoord during the summer, while striker Santiago Gimenez is also returning to Rotterdam after representing Feyenoord between 2022 and 2025.

Feyenoord’s defensive struggles make it difficult to back the hosts with confidence, particularly against a Porto side carrying significantly stronger form and fresh confidence following their dominant victory over Napoli.

While De Kuip remains a challenging venue and Porto’s historical record in the Netherlands is far from convincing, the visitors appear better equipped to handle the pressure of such a crucial European fixture. Given Feyenoord’s recent performances and recurring defensive issues, Porto look capable of taking advantage and securing an important away victory.

Prediction: Sporting Lisbon vs Manchester United

#1746. Man United transfer news: Bruno Fernandes delivers big update on contract talks amid AC Milan links

By Darren Plant | 22 Nov 2026 12:16

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has claimed that it is 'not the right moment' to be talking about a new contract at Old Trafford.

Fernandes will lead out the Red Devils against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday afternoon, with Mauricio Pochettino looking to mark his arrival at Old Trafford with a statement win.

Pochettino has confirmed that the Portuguese will remain as skipper, but reports emerged earlier this week that the playmaker is yet to accept an offer of a new deal.

Should Fernandes pen fresh terms at a time when Man United sit in the relegation zone of the Premier League table, it would represent a major boost for the club.

However, speaking in an interview with Sky Sports, Fernandes has suggested that he has no intention of committing his future to United anytime soon.

While Fernandes spoke positively over club officials making an attempt to extend his contract, he is keen to focus on matters on the pitch.

The former Sporting Lisbon star said: "The club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay.

"There's no negotiations ongoing, but I've seen people saying that 'he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years'. If I wanted more money, I wouldn't be here.

"I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester.

"Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here."

He added: "We spoke about the contract at the end of last season.

"We came in at the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations.

"The most important thing now is that the club gets back to winning games."

Unless Man United move clear of the Premier League relegation zone, it is highly unlikely that Fernandes will be signing a new contract.

That would make no sense for either party, regardless of Fernandes said to have admirers in AC Milan, who are managed by former United boss Ruben Amorim.

United can activate a 12-month option to protect their position, and that feels like the most realistic development over the coming months.

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Charlton are in the midst of a woeful run of form, having won just one of their last 13 Championship matches to leave them six points above the relegation zone.

The Imps have lost their last four games, suffering a late 1-0 defeat to Wrexham on Saturday after Daniel Oyegoke was dispossessed and George Thomason scored a winner.

Lincoln do have the worst home record in the division, having picked up five points from eight games and shipped more goals than any other side, but they have fared better away from home.

Tyrese Campbell and Alli are expected to continue on the wings, with Conor Coventry, Joe Rankin-Costello and Alan Mwamba likely to start in midfield.

#1741. Prediction: Sporting Lisbon vs Manchester United

Manchester United turn their attention back to the Champions League on Wednesday night when they travel to the Estadio Jose Alvalade to face Sporting Lisbon.

The visitors arrive in Portugal reeling from another damaging Premier League defeat, while Sporting are in a much healthier position as they continue their pursuit of a place in the Champions League knockout rounds. At the halfway stage of the league phase, Sporting sit 10th in the 36-team standings, seven places and three points above United.

Sporting have made a solid start to their Champions League campaign and remain firmly in the hunt for automatic qualification.

The Portuguese side have taken nine points from their opening four league-phase matches, recording victories over Galatasaray, Lens and Shakhtar Donetsk. Their only setback came in a disappointing 3-2 home defeat against LASK Linz on matchday three.

Their most recent European outing saw them edge past Shakhtar Donetsk 1-0, and Sporting now head into this fixture under the guidance of new head coach Paulo Fonseca, who has enjoyed a positive start since replacing Rui Borges earlier this month. Sporting have won both matches under his leadership so far.

Before the international break, the Lions claimed a narrow 1-0 Primeira Liga victory over Moreirense, before a heavily rotated side eased to a 4-0 win over fourth-tier Uniao da Serra in the Taca de Portugal on Saturday. Despite those positive results, Sporting remain nine points behind league leaders Porto domestically.

One statistic will particularly encourage the hosts ahead of Wednesday’s clash. Sporting have scored in each of their last 22 Champions League group-stage or league-phase matches, the longest such run by a Portuguese club.

Sporting are hopeful of welcoming back Zeno Debast and Nuno Santos, both of whom are recovering from muscle injuries, although their involvement remains uncertain.

Fonseca is expected to restore several key players to the starting lineup, including Goncalo Inacio, Ivan Fresneda, Issa Doumbia, Rodrigo Zalazar and Geny Catamo. Chelsea loanee Jesse Derry is also pushing for a place in the side.

Colombian striker Luis Suarez is expected to return after being rested at the weekend. He has scored 13 goals in 15 appearances this season, including four in four Champions League matches.

Manchester United make the trip to Portugal searching for a response after a disastrous start to the Mauricio Pochettino era.

The Argentine watched his side suffer a humiliating 4-0 defeat against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, with United reduced to 10 men after Leny Yoro’s controversial early red card. The defeat left the Red Devils 19th in the Premier League table with just eight points, their lowest tally after 11 matches since the 1972-73 season.

Pochettino has publicly acknowledged that the club is involved in a relegation battle and now faces the challenge of tightening a defence that has conceded 34 goals in 16 matches across all competitions this season, more than any other club in Europe’s top five leagues.

European form has been inconsistent for United. They have beaten Sabah and Roma but suffered defeats against Atletico Madrid and Como. The victory over Roma was particularly dramatic, with the Red Devils coming back from two goals down to win 3-2.

United’s away record in the Champions League offers little encouragement. They have won only one of their last 11 away matches in the competition, a 2-0 victory at Villarreal in 2021-22.

There is at least some comfort in the head-to-head record. United have won three of their previous four meetings with Sporting, including both group-stage clashes during their successful 2007-08 Champions League campaign.

United remain without injured trio Manuel Ugarte, Carlos Baleba and Benjamin Sesko. There are also doubts over Marcus Rashford, Luke Shaw and reserve goalkeeper Karl Darlow.

The visitors will definitely be without Matheus Cunha, who is suspended after being sent off in the previous Champions League fixture despite scoring the winning goals against Roma.

Matthijs de Ligt endured a difficult outing against Liverpool and could make way for Harry Maguire, with Pochettino expected to retain a three-man defence alongside Leny Yoro and Lisandro Martinez.

In attack, the absence of Cunha could open the door for either Amad Diallo or Joshua Zirkzee, while captain Bruno Fernandes is set to face Sporting for the first time since leaving the club in January 2020. Fernandes scored 64 goals in 137 appearances for Sporting and has contributed 21 goals in 29 Champions League matches during his career.

Sporting enter the match with greater stability, better form and significantly stronger defensive foundations than their visitors. Fonseca has made a positive start in Lisbon, while the hosts continue to score regularly both domestically and in Europe.

Manchester United are desperately in need of a morale-boosting result, but their defensive issues have shown little sign of improvement and they now face one of the most consistent attacking sides in Portugal. With Sporting boasting strong Champions League form and United struggling badly away from home, the hosts appear well positioned to collect another important three points.

#1740. Glasner made to wait for first win as Trafford thwarts Forest

James Trafford became the record signing for a British goalkeeper this summer and he is already proving invaluable for Leeds United.

Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.

The England international secured his second successive clean sheet in this City Ground sequel to underline why Leeds moved to eclipse the previous record for Jordan Pickford.

“England’s No 1” was a frequent chant from the travelling Leeds fans and although it may take some time for him to dislodge Pickford as the country’s first-choice, he is loving life at his new club.

Trafford produced a number of fine saves and goals from Daniel James and James Justin secured a comfortable Carabao Cup second-round victory for Leeds, who also won here in the league on Saturday.

Dan James has put Leeds ahead against Nottingham Forest 💥 pic.twitter.com/BdiYMXFJ5h

Leeds manager Daniel Farke said: “He has the potential to be one of the best goalkeepers in the Premier League and that is why Thomas Tuchel has picked him for England.

“I like his natural confidence and aura, he knows that he’s good and he will be outstanding one day.

“He has major chances to be under the spotlight and we are very pleased with him so far.”

Forest manager Oliver Glasner will be pleased to see the back of Leeds. He was appointed by Forest for the primary reason of winning trophies after successful tenures with Crystal Palace and Eintracht Frankfurt, but this particular avenue is now closed for this season.

Four-time League Cup winners, Forest endured a difficult evening following the pre-match news that they have agreed a £45m deal with Chelsea for striker Liam Delap.

Forest have established a reputation for noisy transfer windows but are determined to focus on quality over quantity this year. With Delap to undergo a medical on Wednesday, Forest will then focus on signing a new right wing-back before the deadline.

Newcastle’s Jacob Murphy has been discussed, though a move is now regarded as unlikely. There are understood to be other targets under consideration.

Glasner has insisted he does not want Forest to panic, and it remains to be seen whether they do spring into life on the final day. He said: “I am not a magician or the messiah and we cannot ignore the reality that Leeds are ahead of us at the moment.

“For nine months last season we were fighting relegation, so the players know it is going to take a lot of work. I know exactly what we have to change and that is what we will do.

“We are responsible and made so many mistakes. Maybe we needed this result. At the moment we are far away from what we want but we will get there.”

This was a more open game than the attritional encounter from last weekend, as Trafford was forced into a fine early save to prevent Ola Aina’s cross from arcing into the top corner.

Yet both teams were frequently making mistakes and providing masterclasses in how to misplace passes, frustrating their respective managers in the technical area.

The most impressive moment of the first-half came from Leeds centre-back Joe Rodon, racing back into position to deny Chris Wood from close range. Rodon celebrated the tackle as if it were a 30-yard screamer.

It was always likely to be a mistake which proved the pivotal moment, and Arnaud Kalimuendo’s poor header cost the home team in the 50th minute.

Kalimuendo’s error presented Sean Longstaff with space to run into and his pass found James, who beat Matz Sels with a clinical finish.

“Can we play you every week?” was the inevitable chant from the travelling Leeds supporters.

Forest’s fans were becoming twitchy and Trafford produced another save to frustrate Wood from eight yards after a break down the right from Kalimuendo.

Glasner responded by making a quadruple substitution on the hour, yet Leeds remained dangerous and added a second goal 15 minutes from time when Justin bundled home after a goalmouth scramble.

Ethan Ampadu's long throw causes CHAOS in the Forest box as Leeds go 2-0 up! pic.twitter.com/CtGDDIaRNp

You can catch the draw for the next stage of the League Cup on Sky Sports Main Event tomorrow night after the conclusion of Preston North End vs Everton.

Nottingham Forest have agreed a club-record deal worth £45m for Chelsea forward Liam Delap.

Delap has been deemed surplus to requirements at Stamford Bridge, and while the clubs were in talks over an initial loan deal, they have now struck a permanent agreement for the striker.

The 23-year-old​ only signed for Chelsea in a £30m deal from Ipswich Town 12 months ago​ ​and is scheduled for a medical on Wednesday​. He will become Forest’s most expensive signing with the deal eclipsing the £37.5m they paid for Omari Hutchinson last summer.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a new forward and Delap was a long-term target for the Austrian since his time as Crystal Palace head coach.

Delap held talks with Forest last year over a potential move, and was also understood to have spoken with Glasner while he was at Palace.

Speaking to ITV after the win, Rodon said: “I thought we were a bit sharper going forward, maybe a bit naive in the first half. I thought we had a lot of good chances maybe could have scored a couple of goals but we know it’s a difficult place to come and overall very happy to keep a clean sheet and win the game.”

Of his last-ditch tackle in the first half, he added: “We love it, as defenders it’s as good as a goal. I’m delighted, [keeping] clean sheets is my job and overall I got it right in the end.”

"There's a healthy arrogance about Leeds""Farke has gone from strength to strength"Izzy Christiansen and Jobi McAnuff praise the impact of Daniel Farke at Leeds 📈 pic.twitter.com/fgzLWRk3U2

"It's a bit soon to say Wembley!" 😅James Justin and Dan James react to Leeds progressing into round three of the Carabao Cup 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/m81C6eJT7C

Aug 29: Liverpool vs Nottingham ForestSep 5: Nottingham Forest vs Tottenham HotspurSep 12: Aston Villa vs Nottingham ForestSep 19: Nottingham Forest vs CoventryOct 11: Crystal Palace vs Nottingham Forest

Cardiff City 1 Norwich 2Doncaster Rovers 1 Middlesbrough 3Barnsley 3 Crewe Alexandra 2Blackburn Rovers 1 Sheffield United 2Blackpool 1 Lincoln City 4Cambridge United 0 Millwall 1Fleetwood Town 4 Shrewsbury Town 0Ipswich Town 3 Leicester City 1Plymouth 2 Coventry City 4Sheffield Wednesday 0 Wolverhampton Wanderers 2Southampton 1 West Ham United 4Stevenage Town 0 Reading 3Stoke City 1 Hull City 1 (4-5 pens)Walsall 0 Leyton Orient 0 (5-6 pens)Watford 1 Peterborough United 5Birmingham City 1 Brentford 6Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 2

And that is it. Two home defeats by Leeds in less than 80 hours for Forest. Glasner will have much to ponder with a daunting trip to Anfield coming up on Saturday. All smiles for Farke’s side.

A look at a third for Leeds. Aaronson drives forward before setting Wilson who in turn lays on a first-time pass to Calvert-Lewin. The forward attempts to take his shot first time but can’t get the requisite power on the ball to beat Sels.

A pitch invader makes a brief appearance on the turf but is swiftly ushered away.

There is a late chance for Forest. Hutchinson’s cross is helped on by Dominguez but that touch inadvertently takes the ball away from Ndoye at the back post.

Forest fans are filing out of the exits and who can blame them?

That just about sums up Forest’s night. Dominguez stands over a free-kick from a dangerous area and, with the box loaded with their most imposing aerial threats, the midfielder sends the ball well over their heads and out for a goal-kick. So poor.

Calvert-Lewin is now on for Nmecha. Not really the striker Forest defenders would want to see at this stage of the game.

Another set-piece, this time a Stach corner, is barely dealt with by Forest.

There’s a shout for a handball at the other end as Ndoye spears a cross into the body of Elvedi, but the referee rightly waves the appeals away.

The “oles” ring out from the away end as Leeds string a series of passes together in the corner right in front of it. Forest are looking rather helpless here.

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 2 (Justin) Ampadu launches a throw-in from the right but has to reload as the referee notices some pushing in the box. His next attempt is far too loopy but causes Forest all sorts of trouble, bouncing and bobbling, and coming all the way through a thicket of limbs to Nmecha at the far post. Williams attempts to keep the ball out from a prone position on the goalline under pressure from Justin, who gets the final touch as the ball is bundled over the line.

It's messy but Leeds won't care! 😁Forest fail to deal with the throw-in and Nmecha is there to bundle it in...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/oV46fs5RmP

Jair goes into the book after catching Ampadu in full flight. He never had a prayer of reaching that ball.

The resulting free-kick lands to Amapadu himself in the box, but his effort is deflected behind for a corner which is not up to much.

Goalscorer James is taken off for Bogle, who will offer more mettle down Leeds’ right side as Forest search for an equaliser in the closing stages.

Stach has only been on the field for a matter of seconds but comes within a few inches of scoring. Wilson does well on the edge of the box before laying the ball to Stach whose curled effort grazes the outside of the side-netting.

Longstaff’s final contribution to this game is a foul and yellow card as he spreads his legs wide to stop Ndoye breaking away through the middle.

He is replaced by Wilson, as Tanaka and Okafaor also make way, for Stach and Aaronson.

There’s plenty more endeavour down Forest’s new-look left side. Hudson Odoi scampers down that flank before cutting inside, and while he’s unable to fashion a chance the intent is correct.

The substitutions appear to have breathed life into this Forest side. Murillo picks out Dominguez charging forward and Trafford does well to tip the midfielder’s effort behind. The resulting corner comes to nothing.

Glasner resolves he has seen enough and rings the changes. Diomande, Aina, Jesus and Kalimuendo are replaced by Murillo, Netz, Ndoye and Hudson Odoi.

Okafor shows off his dancing feet in the Forest box, pulling off a few stepovers before the ball comes to Ampadu on the edge of the area but his strike is dragged wide.

Chances at both ends! Kalimuendo plays a wonderful ball into the box for Wood to sweep home but Trafford springs into action and makes a stunning save.

Leeds go up the other end, Okafor profiting from a diversionary run from centre-back Elvedi but cannot find the target and double Forest’s lead.

End-to-end football! ⚡️First Wood, then Okafor - just 19 seconds between the two chances 😮#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/TGQmtwLNwE

Leeds are ahead and the inevitable chant from the away supporters is “can we play you every week?”

This is of course their second meeting in four days and Leeds are on course to record the double.

Forest’s fans are starting to get a little twitchy.

Dan James puts Leeds United in front! ⚽️Tidy finish from the Welshman... #EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/GzWg6zLGLm

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 1 (James) We finally have a breakthrough. Kalimuendo gives the ball up cheaply in the middle of the park and Longstaff is there to pick up the pieces, darting infield before laying on a perfectly weighted for James to gallop on to, take a touch and sweep beyond Sels. The winger has been Leeds’ biggest threat and deserves that goal.

James finds space down the right - again - and his cross is closed down and deflected behind for a corner.

Longstaff’s floated delivery is tipped away by Sels, but it turns out that the ball went out before coming in so a Forest goal kick is awarded.

A lovely rendition of Mull of Kintyre precedes a short blast of the referee’s whistle and we’re back under way...

Schlager goes into the book instantly for grabbing a handful of Tanaka’s shirt as the Japan international attempted to escape his clutches.

This hasn’t been much of an improvement from Saturday.

Both teams are producing masterclasses in how to misplace passes. Oliver Glasner and Daniel Farke have spent much of the first half looking very frustrated.

James Trafford must be feeling very comfortable and confident of a second successive clean sheet after joining from Manchester City.

Let’s hope for an improvement in the second-half.

Should the scores remain level after 90 minutes, we will go straight to penalties. There’s still a half to play of course, but Forest’s League Cup shoot-out record should be a source of confidence having won seven from eight.

What a tackle from Joe Rodon! 💥#EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/p5GkzSFEoZ

James wins the ball on the halfway line and feeds Okafor down the left. He attempts a deft through-ball into a thicket of bodies but it comes to nothing.

Leeds circulate the ball, working the ball from side to side but there is nowhere near enough movement in front of the ball-player for any meaningful forward passes to be played.

And, quite aptly, the referee blows up at three seconds past 45 minutes. Certainly not a half for the books.

Another half-chance for Forest! Milenkovic lands on a second ball off a deep free-kick but he cannot keep his strike down. A classic centre-half’s effort if you will.

Ampadu comes over to the left to fire in a long throw-in. Sels comes steaming out of his goal and fumbles the ball but is awarded a free-kick after Muharemovic makes contact. Looked very minimal in all fairness.

Oof, a good chance for Aina! Williams’ cross from the left comes all the way through to his opposite wing-back, but Aina’s half-volley sails over. A cracking contact, though.

Elvedi and Muharemovic look to be astute buys from Leeds’ perspective. Both assured at the back and the latter especially is confident progressing the ball.

Just as I type that Forest threaten with a ball over the top, but Justin nips in to take the ball away from Wood.

Another decent opening for Leeds after a Forest turnover. Nmecha strides through the middle but Milenkovic is in position to ensure his run comes to nothing.

What a tackle! Kalimuendo bursts through the middle after Leeds cede possession in a dangerous position. The winger plays in Wood who looks to be through on goal but Rodon comes out of nowhere to telescope a limb and stop the forward in his tracks. Fantastic defensive work from the Welshman.

Nmecha attempts to break beyond the halfway line but is stymied by a swarm of Forest players. He demands a foul from the referee who is not interested in the least.

It’s then Okafor’s turn to put in a dangerous cross from the left, but Nmecha cannot get to it.

Tanaka becomes the first man to go into the book. The ball gets away from him and Jesus puts body between man and ball smartly to win the foul.

Tanaka is now dropping into the back line to allow Leeds’ defenders the licence to get wider and higher. Forest will need to be wary of their opponents’ numerical advantage down the flanks.

The game has reached something of a holding pattern as both sides resolve to slow things down, at least temporarily. Forest have settled into a slightly deeper block.

Sensing an opportunity, Ampadu spins in a glorious through-ball between centre-back and full-back for James to gallop on to. He hits the by-line and cuts back to Longstaff, but the midfielder can’t beat Sels. A good chance that probably should have been converted.

A good chance goes begging! 🫣Longstaff is free for Leeds but fires it straight at Sels...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/0UJdfSDQ6w

Tanaka then turns provider, winning possession in Forest’s half before playing in Longstaff, whose cross-cum-shot does not threaten Sels’ goal.

Both sides have physical, quick out-balls, which has made for a frenetic encounter thus far. James rasps in another fierce cross from the right after another sweeping Leeds move, but Nmecha cannot get there and Tanaka fires well over on the follow-up.

Aina’s throw-in, this time from the left, is flicked on to Jesus at the back post and while the forward is able to direct the ball goalwards there is Justin on the line to clear the ball to safety.

Chance! Dominguez slides in Aina down the right channel and the full-back’s mishit cross has Trafford scrambling. He palms the ball behind for a corner, which is headed away for a Forest throw-in on the far side.

Leeds are enjoying a spell of possession here, Tanaka and Longstaff peeling off into the wide areas to collect the ball and disrupt Forest’s mid-block out-of-possession structure. The hosts are more than happy for Leeds to circulate the ball in front of their first line of pressure as, for the second time tonight, Trafford boots it out into touch.

Dominguez stands up a smart cross to the far post where Aina is waiting to head back across goal. Trafford backpedals into Kalimuendo and the referee awards Leeds a free-kick.

Wonderful touch there early in the game from none other than Oliver Glasner.

Forest’s head coach perfectly trapped a high ball as it landed towards him in the technical area.

James shows off his speed for the first time tonight, accelerating down the right before fizzing a dangerous ball into the six-yard box but Forest clear their lines.

Sels goes long to Wood (feels like the right play given his attributes), James lands on the second ball but can only boot the ball into row Z to jeers from the home fans.

Aina launches a long throw-in from the right and it’s headed behind for a corner. Trafford punches the inswinging delivery away and Williams’ effort from the edge of the box sails well over.

Forest are in their red home shirts, kicking from left to right. Leeds are in their yellow away number. Same set-up as the weekend.

Players and mascots walk on to the City Ground turf. A place in the League Cup third round on the line.

Cardiff City vs NorwichDoncaster Rovers vs MiddlesbroughBarnsley vs Crewe AlexandraBlackburn Rovers vs Sheffield UnitedBlackpool vs Lincoln CityCambridge United vs MillwallFleetwood Town vs Shrewsbury TownIpswich Town vs Leicester CityPlymouth vs Coventry CitySheffield Wednesday vs Wolverhampton WanderersSouthampton vs West Ham United Stevenage Town vs ReadingStoke City vs Hull City Walsall vs Leyton OrientWatford Peterborough UnitedBirmingham City vs BrentfordNottingham Forest vs Leeds United

The first pre-match question put to Glasner by ITV was in relation to the reported £45m club-record deal for Chelsea forward Liam Delap. He responded: “I can tell everybody that he doesn’t play today. Everything else we shall see in the next days.”

Oliver Glasner breaks his silence on Nottingham Forest's record signing, Liam Delap 🚨He speaks to @gabrielclarke05 ahead of Forest's Carabao Cup tie against Leeds 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/8DlWMIzVS9

Reflecting on Saturday’s defeat by Leeds in his programme notes, Glasner wrote: “I saw plenty of encouraging signs from the team on Saturday and I felt we were a lot closer to scoring than we were conceding, especially in the second half. Unfortunately, the small margins were not on our side.

“I thought our defence looked comfortable, but there is still work to be done and the more the players get used to the system we’re operating, the more we’ll see that work come to fruition in competitive matches.

“We have recovered well and will be ready to give our all this evening.”

Previewing tonight’s League Cup match, Leeds head coach Daniel Farke said: “Our league win is good for our mood and confidence, but this is a ‘do or die’ cup game. Both teams will be motivated to progress, so I expect a tight game. It will be difficult to win on the road again against a tough opponent.”

When asked what winning a first trophy of his managerial career would mean to him, Farke added: “Well, we weren’t too far away last season. Overall, I would say my form in cup competitions hasn’t been too bad during my career. I’m a big believer in these competitions, I like the ‘do or die’ mentality. I would never say no to another good cup run.”

The hosts’ kits tonight will include Carabao Cup sleeve patches with the number four on them, in recognition of the club’s League Cup triumphs in 1978, 1979, 1989 and 1990.

This is Forest and Leeds Part 2, just four days after they clashed in the Premier League.

Daniel Farke ruined the Oliver Glasner welcoming party on Saturday with a 1-0 smash-and-grab victory at the death.

Both managers have gone relatively strong for this tie, with only a sprinkling of debuts.

Ousmane Diomande, the £34m signing from Sporting, makes his first appearance while there is a first start for Xaver Schlager.

Leeds have given a debut to Switzerland defender Nico Elvedi.

Nottingham Forest Sels; Diomande, Jair, Milenkovic; Aina, Schlager, Dominguez, Williams; Jesus, Kalimuendo; Wood

Subs Victor, Murillo, Abbott, Netz, Hutchinson, Ndoye, McAtee, Sangare, Hudson Odoi

Leeds United Trafford; Rodon, Elvedi, Muharemovic; Ampadu, Tanaka, Longstaff, Justin; James, Okafor; Nmecha

Subs Perri, Lienou, Bijol, Bogle, Wilson, Cresswell, Stach, Aaronson, Calvert-Lewin

The big breaking news is that Forest are smashing their club record to sign Chelsea forward Liam Delap for £45m.

Delap will undergo a medical at Forest on Wednesday with the deal potentially rising to £50m after add-ons.

It eclipses the previous transfer record of £37.5m for winger Omari Hutchinson.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a new centre-forward this summer and Delap ticks pretty much every box for him.

Farke makes six changes to the complement that started against Forest in the league on Saturday.

📋 Your #LUFC XI... pic.twitter.com/XuUzwwkmfi

Wood makes Glasner’s XI while summer acquisitions Diomande and Schlager are handed their first competitive Forest starts.

Our @Carabao_Cup XI this evening. 📋 pic.twitter.com/Wv918WJScj

Welcome to live coverage of the Carabao Cup second-round match between Nottingham Forest and Leeds United. This will be the sides’ second meeting at the City Ground in four days after Anton Stach’s late free-kick decided an attritional contest on the Premier League’s opening weekend. Forest’s new head coach Oliver Glasner is something of a cup specialist, though, with FA Cup, Europa League and Conference League titles to his name and he will relish the opportunity to right the wrongs of Saturday in front of the Forest faithful.

The Austrian is Forest’s fifth head coach in less than 12 months and he will look to arrest the churn by bringing to the City Ground the success he enjoyed with Crystal Palace. During pre-season, the Austrian moulded Forest into his preferred 3-4-3 shape, placing summer acquisition Ousmane Diomande alongside the existing central-defensive partnership of Murillo and Nikola Milenković. Here, Diomande gets his Forest debut and Glasner brings in talisman Chris Wood from the start.

Daniel Farke will have been delighted to see his Leeds side continue their excellent form in pre-season – which included victories over Liverpool, Red Bull Leipzig and Augsburg – into the season proper. Although Leeds arrive at the City Ground shorn of attacking options Wilfried Gnonto, Noah Okafor and Mateo Joseph through injury, Farke still shuffles the pack in the forward positions with this weekend’s visit of Brentford to Elland Road in mind.

#1739. GdS: Tough skin and Dzeko precedent – Ramos has time to reverse flop status

Goncalo Ramos has struggled to find the back of the net with the AC Milan shirt so far, with the Rossoneri hoping that he will eventually find his groove.

After years of struggling in the No.9 position, following the departure of Olivier Giroud, Gerry Cardinale said enough is enough and spent over €70m on Ramos this summer. However, at least so far, it seems that wasn’t the right solution after all.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Portuguese striker has only scored three goals for the Rossoneri so far, despite featuring in every single game except one. Meanwhile, Alphadjo Cisse has eight goals to his name and cost almost ten times less than the No.9.

As highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport, if we were to conduct a survey today, Ramos would be the undisputed leader of seasonal flops for many. The fact that Milan are even considering investing another €50m+ in another striker says a lot.

Of course, such a move shouldn’t be seen as the Rossoneri demonstrating their lack of confidence in the striker. On the contrary, since Cardinale wants to aim for the Scudetto, having two very strong strikers would only be natural.

Still, Ramos needs to step up his goalscoring either way. The hard work he puts in every game, while recognised by the fans, isn’t enough as the usual “that’s not what a striker should do” always follows that praise. The old cliché is true: for strikers, scoring goals is the most important thing.

As the pink newspaper continues, given their characteristics and quality on the ball, Edin Dzeko is a good precedent for Ramos to cling to. The Bosnian arrived in Rome from Manchester City and struggled a bit in his first season (eight league goals), causing a headache for everyone involved.

However, in the following season, he bagged a whopping 29 league goals with the help of Luciano Spalletti’s trust and the assists from Francesco Totti and Mohamed Salah. His resurgence was remarkable, so it’s something Ramos can take inspiration from.

#1738. Portsmouth vs West Ham United - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 22 Nov 2026 12:56, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 10:06

West Ham United will travel to Fratton Park for the first time in 14 years for Tuesday's Championship clash against Portsmouth.

The Hammers head into the midweek round of fixtures in 10th place, while the hosts are a point behind in 12th spot in the Championship table.

Portsmouth are sitting four points adrift of the top eight after winning six, drawing five and losing five of their 16 league games this term.

Pompey put together a six-game unbeaten run before they fell to a narrow 2-1 defeat in their most recent home outing before the international break.

John Mousinho's side then returned to action with an underwhelming display in Saturday's 1-1 away draw against Bolton Wanderers, which saw Josh Murphy score the opener with what proved to be Pompey's only shot on target.

Murphy's first goal since March 2025 was soon called out by Sam Dalby as Portsmouth played out a third consecutive away draw after previously taking a point from trips to Wolverhampton Wanderers and Burnley.

Portsmouth will now return to the familiar surroundings of Fratton Park, where they have won four of their last six outings since losing their opening two home games.

That said, they will be looking to tighten up their backline if they are to take anything off the league's highest scorers, having recorded just one clean sheet in their eight outings at Fratton Park

Meanwhile, West Ham have significant work to do if they are to secure an immediate return to the Premier League in their first Championship campaign since 2011-12.

The West Ham hierarchy took the decision to sack Nuno Espirito Santo after being underwhelmed by a return of six wins from the opening 13 league matches of the season.

Former Hammers midfielder Scott Parker has since taken over the reins, but he is still waiting to secure his first win after over two draws and one defeat in his first three matches.

After starting his reign with a comeback 3-3 draw against Cardiff City, Parker saw his side fall to a narrow 2-1 loss against Blackburn Rovers, before his charges returned from the international break with a frustrating 1-1 draw against Championship's basement side Preston North End.

As a result, West Ham have now gone five games without a win since recording back-to-back away victories over Lincoln City and Swansea City, leaving them three points adrift of the playoff spots and eight points away from the top two.

In search of inspiration, the Hammers can take confidence from the fact they have already beaten Portsmouth at home in the EFL Cup this season, and have won two of their previous three head-to-head away games - a 4-1 success in December 2008 (a game that Parker started) and a 1-0 victory in January 2012.

Portsmouth’s lengthy absentee list features Marko Milovanovic, Colby Bishop, Luke Brooke-Smith, Keshi Anderson, John Swift, Mark Kosznovszky, Benjamin Arthur and Connor Ogilvie.

Jayden Meghoma is a doubt after being forced off in the closing stages against Bolton with an ankle problem, while a calf issue prevented Marlon Pack from starting Saturday’s draw.

Mousinho will welcome back midfielder Ebou Adams, who has served his one-match ban for an accumulation of yellow cards.

As for the visitors, they are unable to call upon Kyle Walker-Peters and Keiber LaMadrid due to muscle and knee problems respectively.

Goalkeeper Alphonse Areola remains a doubt after sitting out Saturday’s draw with an injury he sustained in the pre-match warm-up against Blackburn earlier this month.

Defender Max Kilman is expected to come into the back four after completing his one-match suspension for accumulating five yellow cards in the Championship.

Schmid; Devlin, Poole, Dia, Swanson; Adams, Mohamed; Segecic, Bailey, Kamara; Shade

West Ham United possible starting lineup:

Herrick; Veltman, Mavropanos, Kilman, Mayers; Alvarez; Bowen, Engels, Mukasa, Solomon; Taty

While West Ham lost their last away game against Blackburn, that result represents their only defeat in their eight Championship road trips this season, so we expect them to take something from this midweek encounter.

However, we think they will be forced to settle for a point against a Portsmouth side that has lost just one of their previous eight matches.

#1737. The Chelsea problem Xabi Alonso cannot ignore - and who is really to blame

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

There is no defending Chelsea, because again there was simply no defending by Chelsea.

One goal up and with home advantage against a Leeds team they had already beaten at Stamford Bridge this season in the Carabao Cup, Xabi Alonso and his players took that encouraging platform for success and ripped it up, deservedly losing 4-1.

At least Mauricio Pochettino and Manchester United could play the “we only had 10 men” card.

Whatever is failing to function right now at Chelsea is a complex web spun by poor decision-making and performances from a whole host of implicated parties.

The Chelsea defence showcases the Blues’ endemic struggles for consistency in a perfect microcosmic form, not least because there are so many stakeholders who must each accept their share of the blame.

An injury record peculiarly problematic for a team largely only playing once a week this season in the absence of any European football has left them without captain Reece James, summer signing Maxence Lacroix and the improved Jorrel Hato - players whose availability might not cure all their defensive ills, but would certainly help.

Their absences mean more minutes for players not showing any signs that they possess the composure or robustness needed to provide support for a potent attack and secure a return to the Champions League.

Malo Gusto was beaten twice for Brenden Aaronson’s run to goal for Leeds’ fourth - something that happens all too often for a player valued by Chelsea at £75million in the summer transfer market.

Wesley Fofana remains a liability, and his £75m transfer fee back in 2022 - £89.2m adjusted for inflation - surely makes him the worst pound-for-pound signing Chelsea have made in the BlueCo era.

And while Josh Acheampong, 20, has been the one Chelsea defender to draw consistent praise in the first three months of the campaign, he was suspect against Leeds.

So too was Levi Colwill, a player with enormous potential but who has so far failed to rediscover his physicality and form since the torn anterior cruciate ligament that kept him sidelined for almost all of last season.

A question it is worth Alonso and his coaching staff asking themselves: is 34-year-old Emi Martinez clearly a better goalkeeper than Mike Penders, the inevitable long-term No1?

New details emerge as Chelsea star ‘robbed’ after Leeds game

Transfer news LIVE: Shock Arsenal move; Man Utd striker deal

Chelsea get new Rogers penalty review after Leeds handball controversy

Art After Dark is back with an exciting calendar of cultural events

There is a case to be made to fully blood Penders now, whatever promises might have been made to Martinez when he joined. The Argentine currently looks a shadow of the commanding player he was at Aston Villa.

Wesley Fofana must surely be Chelsea’s worst pound-for-pound signing in the BlueCo era

Individual errors from Fofana and Gusto and the softness of Colwill and Martinez mean plenty of the blame is rightly being portioned in their direction, but other parties are just as culpable.

Alonso, for example, has flattered to deceive as manager so far, switching between a back three and a back four with the result that his team look capable of playing neither, not both. His Chelsea side have scored a laudable 20 league goals but conceded a lamentable 20 at the other end.

Responsibility also lies at the boardroom door, where questionable recruitment has taken place. Benoit Badiashile and Axel Disasi were not at the standard required and have taken too long to move on (still neither player has permanently left the club).

And while he is far from the complete product, Trevoh Chalobah had been one of the more consistent centre-backs of the Clearlake era yet was moved on to high-flying Como this summer in favour of handing a greater amount of game time to Fofana.

If Chelsea are to get back to the pinnacle of English football, which is where the club sees itself, then recruitment, coaching and player performances must all improve.

Accepting shared responsibility is the first step towards revamping and properly rebuilding a defence that simply isn’t going to deliver Champions League football on current form.

Bruno Fernandes has revealed that talks over a new Manchester United contract have ended.

But the decision has been made to put discussions on hold as he believes the club's priority should be returning to winning ways.

"Yeah, the club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay,” he told Sky Sports.

I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations

"We spoke about the contract at the end of last season, we came in the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side.

“I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations because the most important thing now is that the club gets back to win games."

#1735. Spurs transfer news: Can Mikey Moore be recalled from FC Koln in January?

By Darren Plant | 22 Nov 2026 13:07

Tottenham Hotspur allegedly do not have the option to recall Mikey Moore from his loan at FC Koln.

Spurs' 2-0 victory over Ipswich Town on Saturday afternoon has moved the club into ninth place in the Premier League table.

With a squad possessing depth and a schedule that lacks European football, Roberto De Zerbi is not exactly in desperate need of additions during the winter transfer window.

Nevertheless, academy graduate Moore is earning regular football in Germany, seemingly putting him in the thoughts of the Italian.

However, as per talkSPORT, Spurs may have to wait until the summer to reintegrate the winger.

Moore made the headlines on Friday courtesy of scoring for FC Koln against Bayern Munich in the Bundesliga.

The 19-year-old's early effort at the Allianz Arena helped earn his side a 1-1 draw against the champions.

That goal was Moore's first in six starts and three substitute outings in Germany's top flight.

Nevertheless, Spurs are seemingly not in the position to automatically recall Moore should they wish to do so.

With Moore having already represented Spurs this season, he can only play for his parent club or Koln for the remainder of the campaign.

If Spurs earn a return to European football for 2027-28, Moore's homegrown status means that he will likely be used in De Zerbi's squad.

For now, though, it makes sense that he is playing a key role for Koln, who sit in 13th place in the Bundesliga table.

Should he continue to accumulate regular minutes, it will stand him in good stead for next season.

#1734. Amorim discusses ‘fun’ Frosinone, final third struggles and confirms Pavlovic’s return

On the eve of AC Milan’s game against Frosinone, Ruben Amorim spoke to the media at the usual pre-match press conference.

The international break is officially over and Milan will be back in action tomorrow. After wins against Inter and Genoa, the goal is to make it three consecutive wins, although an in-form Frosinone side will be looking to make life difficult for them.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Amorim’s plan appears to be to field an attacking-minded starting eleven, picking up where he left off against Genoa. It’s certainly a bold plan as Frosinone will surely look to cause issues on the counter, as also highlighted by Oliver in his prediction.

Speaking to the media at Milanello, Amorim shared his thoughts on the game, the status of the players after the international break, and the tactical solutions moving forward.

“We as a club have a big responsibility. Fondazione Milan is really important because it reflects our values and helps the community. Our doors are always open for everyone. It’s also good for the players to see and live different realities.”

“I think everyone is ready. Of course, we had to control the load during the week, because some of them travelled a lot. I’m really pleased with our players getting game time, because that’s the best way to maintain, so we are ready for the game.”

On Pavlovic’s status and Frosinone’s style..

“Starting with Pavlovic, he’s doing better. He will be in the squad. I don’t know if he will start or not, so I will see. He wants to play and I want him to play. We miss that fire that he has. Let’s see, but for sure he will be in the team.

“Frosinone are fun to watch, they are the team that runs the most, and we are second so I think we can fight that. They are really good with 1v1s on the flanks. If you watch their games it’s hard to understand their movement. There is some logic in their chaos, but it’s hard to spot.

“They play a different style, more direct, which allows them to have the ball more inside the box. So it’s going to be a really hard game. As I said against Venezia, there are some teams that we need to be really focused against because their styles can cause issues.”

Camarda is getting little game time, despite the Ramos struggles. Is a strong deputy striker missing?

“Two different questions. Of course we can say that one more option would be a good thing, but I think the struggles of Ramos are the struggles of the team. We are not reaching the final third, we are one of the worst teams in that sense. So we don’t have a lot of shots.

“I don’t want loads of shots outside the box, because it’s hard to score with those. We need to get into the box and we are not helping Ramos. What I saw against Genoa is that without Ramos, we wouldn’t have scored those goals. But again, we need to do better in the final third, my goal is to push the team forward. That’s my job.

“It’s true that he’s working hard and doing a lot of good. I know that it’s not his sole job to press, we spent a lot of money on a player to score goals, but we are not doing enough to help him. We need to push the team forward.”

Are you happy with the league standings so far? And against Genoa, you basically played with four attacking players. Can this be a solution for the future?

“Starting with the last question, it depends on the opponents and the moment of the team. I don’t believe that playing with more attackers means you will reach the final third more. Sometimes you get that effect from having more midfielders, for example. We are always going to change in some matches depending on the opponent.

“On the first question, it’s difficult to say. I think that we have grown as a team quite fast, but I’m not pleased with the overall situation. We need to be so much better and as such, I’m not pleased with where we are in the standings. But of course, I need to say that I’m happy with how the players have worked.”

During the break, we saw Camarda scoring for the U21s. Could a loan be the right solution?

“I was a young player myself once too. A young player wants everything really badly, which is a good thing. That said, he needs time to adapt, it’s really hard to play for a club like Milan. You just said there is pressure on Ramos, imagine what it’s like for Camarda.

“I don’t know what will happen in January, but he needs to be focused on these games. Everything can change in just a few weeks.

“I’m really happy with how he has been since he returned from international duty, I heard that Baldini spoke with him at length (as Baldini said himself), and he returned in a happier mood. I understand the question about January, but January is so far away right now.”

The feeling is that the team is struggling to keep control at the end of the games…

“Sometimes even when we are winning, we have dropped the levels in every action of the game. I think we are controlling everything better, you saw it in the second half against Genoa without spending a lot of energy, but I think it’s all connected to the attack.

“If we don’t create danger when we are leading, we will struggle a bit to kill the games. Of course, we need to address that and we are working on it.”

On Musah as a left-back and if more versatile players will be signed…

“That was a specific situation. I don’t know and I’m not going to tell you guys what we are thinking about January. I wanted a right-footed player against Genoa. You saw the runs of Rabiot, so I wanted someone right-footed to pass the ball on immediately.

“Musah is not going to play as a left-back tomorrow, I can tell you that, but it’s an option. I like to have players who can play in several positions.”

“I think it helps any player to feel the confidence from the club. I think it’s clear that was done with the new contract. Then I also told you when he wasn’t playing that he’s really important for us. I can tell you today that Pulisic perhaps is the one player we cannot replace.

“The movement in between the lines he brings, we simply don’t have another Pulisic. His absence is always felt a lot, so from that you can understand how important he is for us. He doesn’t talk a lot, but he lets the pitch do the talking.

“I would put him in the same category as Rabiot. Players who are on another level. I don’t like speaking about individuals, but I think everyone can see this.”

Can the January transfer window serve to raise the team’s ambition?

“That is the biggest mistake of the big clubs. Looking at the table and deciding whether to invest or not. I think the key is to have a long-term plan. Stick with your plan. We have one and everything is very clear.

“Trying to become a champion by spending money is the biggest mistake. The key is following your plan. I look at the table to evaluate the process as a whole, not to decide whether to spend a lot on signings.”

Are you keeping track of your players so they don’t stay up late at night playing GTA?

“I will let my friend Gennaro Gattuso respond. Jokes aside, I don’t care.”

Is a winner a dreamer who never gives up? Are you a dreamer?

“I wouldn’t call it a dream but the goal is to win every game. If you look at my journey, every club I chose, I clearly am a dreamer [laughs]. I really want to be part of this club for the rest of my career, but I also know that I need to prove myself.

“I’m a dreamer, yes, but also very focused on the goal.”

Arsenal have a nervous wait to discover if David Raya is set for a spell on the sidelines.

#1732. De Zerbi claims Marseille used him as ‘scapegoat’

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Roberto De Zerbi accused former club Marseille of using him as a "scapegoat" despite him giving "everything" for them.

De Zerbi took charge of Marseille in June 2024 on a three-year contract and led them to a second-place finish in Ligue 1 in his debut campaign.

He also came within seconds of winning the Trophee des Champions in the following campaign, but Goncalo Ramos scored a 95th-minute equaliser for Paris Saint-Germain to take the game to penalties, and Marseille lost the shootout.

De Zerbi's tenure did not last much longer after that; a Champions League league-phase exit was followed by a 5-0 Classique hammering, which resulted in his departure in February.

The Italian was not out of a job for long, signing with Tottenham at the end of March, but he has now hit out at Marseille for what he feels was unjust treatment.

"Many times, I was the scapegoat for everyone, but in such an important club and city, everyone has to take responsibility, not just a few people, of whom I was one," De Zerbi told Canal+, as quoted by TNT Sports.

"I'm sorry, because when I signed for Marseille, I wanted it so badly and I thought I would stay for many years.

"However, some people didn't keep their word to me. They told me things they didn't follow through on. A year and a half had passed before the Champions Trophy in Kuwait.

"We were on the verge of winning a title after a 12-year drought. Since that match, the situation deteriorated; it worsened until my departure.

"Marseille is one of the clubs I hold closest to my heart, along with Foggia. I suffered a lot when I left. I suffered because I gave everything in Marseille."

Moving forward as one https://t.co/NSYHCeV5Wp

— Tottenham Hotspur (@SpursOfficial) November 21, 2026

De Zerbi has impressed since arriving at Spurs, ensuring they kept their Premier League status on the last day of the 2025-26 season.

Though they failed to win their first six Premier League games this term, they have since lost just one of their last five (W4) to move them up to ninth in the table.

However, he has admitted he does not see himself remaining in coaching for a long time, as he is keen to explore life outside of football, though he is in no hurry to leave the dugout just yet.

"I don't think I'll stay in football much longer. Your life revolves around football, but life isn't just that," he added.

"That time hasn't come yet. For me, being a coach at this level is already a dream.

"I don't measure dreams by the titles won, but more by the human impact you have. I always want to stay the same and always look people in the eye. Even when I make mistakes, because I make a lot of them."

#1731. Slovan Bratislava vs Real Betis - prediction, team news, lineups

By Saikat Mandal | 22 Nov 2026 13:13, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 10:08

Slovan Bratislava will be looking to secure their first victory of the 2026-27 Champions League campaign when they host Real Betis at Tehelne Pole Stadion on Tuesday.

The Sky Blues sit bottom of the league phase table with no points from four matches, while Betis occupy 11th place with nine points.

Slovan defeated Celje away from home in the second leg of their playoff-round tie to secure a place in the Champions League main phase, marking a historic achievement for the club.

However, the Slovakian side have found the step up in quality difficult to handle, losing all four of their matches, scoring just once and conceding 17 goals.

Yaya Toure's side began their campaign with a heavy 6-1 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain before suffering further losses against Stuttgart, Roma and LASK.

Balancing their domestic and European commitments has also proved challenging, with their continental struggles seemingly affecting their league form, as they sit second in the Slovakian top flight, seven points behind leaders DAC 1904 despite having played a game more.

Perhaps most frustrating for Toure is Slovan's poor home form, with the Sky Blues winless in their last five matches at Tehelne Pole Stadion, drawing three of those encounters.

Real Betis have made a solid start to their European campaign, collecting three wins from four matches while scoring eight goals and conceding six.

El Glorioso opened their campaign with a hard-fought 3-2 victory over Lille, coming from behind to claim all three points.

They followed that up with another thrilling 3-2 win against Porto before beating Feyenoord 1-0 to secure back-to-back home victories.

Manuel Pellegrini's side suffered a narrow 2-1 defeat to Borussia Dortmund in their previous Champions League outing, but they have an excellent opportunity to climb the table with a victory over Slovan.

Betis are unbeaten in their last three matches across all competitions and head into this encounter on the back of a 1-1 draw against city rivals Sevilla in La Liga.

Slovan Bratislava form (all competitions):

The switch from a 3-4-3 to a 4-1-4-1 formation has helped Slovan pick up a draw and a victory in their last two matches, and Toure is likely to stick with the same system.

The back four of Sandro Cruz, Svetozar Markovic, Kenan Bajric and Daiki Matsuoka are expected to retain their places, with Peter Pokorny operating at the base of midfield.

Artur Gajdos appeared to pick up an injury in the previous game and could be replaced by Alexej Maros, while Andraz Sporar is set to continue up front, with Roman Cerepaki a doubt due to a back problem.

Real Betis are likely to be without Dani Ceballos, who is currently sidelined with a hamstring problem and is not expected to return to action before the start of December.

Fran Garcia and Hector Bellerin are expected to retain their places in defence, while Diego Llorente could come into the side in place of Marc Bartra.

Antony picked up a knock in the derby but he has travelled with the squad, and should retain his place alongside Isco and Abdessamad Ezzalzouli, with Jose Antonio Morante currently sidelined through injury.

Slovan Bratislava possible starting lineup:

Popovic; Cruz, Markovic, Bajric, Matsuoka; Pokomy, Barseghyan, Ibrahim, Maros, Marcelli; Sporar

Valles; Garcia, Natan, Llorente, Bellerin; Fornals, Bernal; Ezzalzouli, Isco, Antony; Parrott

Slovan have looked like fish out of water in the Champions League this season, and it would take a herculean effort for them to get anything from this encounter, although we expect the hosts to put up a better fight.

Real Betis, meanwhile, have been flying in Europe this season and should be confident of securing their second away victory in the competition as they look to bounce back from their defeat against Dortmund.

#1730. Di Marzio: Cagliari could give Milan a ‘buy option’ for Mendy to secure Camarda loan

Francesco Camarda could join Cagliari on loan in January and as part of the deal, AC Milan could obtain an option for Paul Mendy, according to a report.

There has been a lot of speculation regarding Camarda’s future in the last few weeks. The 18-year-old has played just 119 minutes so far this season and it’s clear that his development isn’t moving in the right direction as a result.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

A loan seems to be the most likely option, especially if Milan were to bring in another striker, but the big question is where he should go. After a so-so loan spell at Lecce, the Rossoneri must evaluate carefully before making their choice.

According to Gianluca Di Marzio, Cagliari have expressed a concrete interest in securing Camarda on a loan with an option to buy, leaving a buy-back in favour of Milan. In other words, it would be the same formula that was used when he moved to Lecce.

There is one big difference, though. As per the journalist, the Cagliari striker Paul Mendy could also be involved in the deal. The idea would be to add a ‘buy option’ for Milan, presumably giving them priority to sign the player for a pre-agreed fee.

The 19-year-old has bagged two goals and two assists for the Sardinian side so far, attracting the interest of several clubs (and not just Milan).

#1729. Jamie Carragher issues Manchester United relegation verdict after Liverpool defeat

Jamie Carragher believes that Manchester United face a fight to stay in the Premier League.

The Red Devils remain mired in the top flight’s relegation zone after their heavy 4-0 defeat by Liverpool on Sunday, which saw a nightmare debut for new manager Mauricio Pochettino.

The Argentine, who began work at Carrington last Wednesday, watched on in horror as his new side were outplayed from the off at Anfield, with Leny Yoro sent off inside eight minutes for hauling down Alexander Isak, who was clean through on goal.

Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz got the goals to round off the rout on Merseyside, and it leaves United with just one win in 12 matches in all competitions.

On Sky Sports, Carragher said: “They’re in a relegation fight right now because of where they are in the table. You can’t say anything else when you look at their record this season.

“If the name wasn’t Manchester United and you’re watching the performances, you’d say that is a team that’s in a relegation fight. They’re conceding lots of goals, comedy of errors, red cards, they’ve won one game all season – that is a team in a relegation fight.

“We don’t believe it will happen over a 38-game season but they haven’t had the most difficult of starts. They’ve played a lot of promoted teams, they haven’t played the best team in the league Arsenal yet.

“I don’t think they’ll go down, but this idea that they haven’t got a scrap on their hands- they have.”
