This is exactly what the youth academy is there for, and itai??i??s very pleasing to see Klopp isnai??i??t ignoring it and focusing on the transfer market. That being said, itai??i??s not as if the German should never sign a player. In the transfer market, there are 3 types of signings — the doai??i??s, the donai??i??ts, and the ones you sign only if you absolutely have to.

So then, thereai??i??s only two possible types of players Liverpool should be buying in the winter window:

In the summer windows, one can look at options beyond these two. Your scouting team can have a list of targets, clubs are more open to listening to offers, and you have an opportunity to move out some of your own players to make room for signings. You also have a solid pre-season ahead, so that players who might need to be brought up to speed on the teamai??i??s style of play can be worked with before theyai??i??re thrown into the deep end. January simply isnai??i??t the right time for all this.

So what kind of signings should be avoided? Letai??i??s just call them the a Southampton signingsai??i??. These are the so-called a Premier League readyai??i?? players who seem like an improved version of the current squad, mostly based on their performances in the current season. Some examples of such players would be the likes of Saido Mane, Marko Arnautovic, and Riyad Mahrez. All 3 are talented players, and on paper would make good additions to a side that has not performed well in front of goal. But one good season does not a good player make. Keep in mind that Christian Benteke, Adam Lallana, Dejan Lovren and Roberto Firmino were all their former clubsai??i?? best players, and highly coveted at the time, but none of them have been instant hits at Merseyside. Therefore, to imagine that a January signing will suddenly improve your season is misguided, and you end up paying over the odds as most clubs donai??i??t want to lose their best players mid-way through the season.

One recent transfer rumour has linked Alexandre Pato to a move to Merseyside. What a pointless and risky transfer this would be. Liverpool already have 4 senior strikers on their rolls, excluding Roberto Firmino who can also play up front. Other than Daniel Sturridge, who is one day elder to Pato, all the other 3 are younger than the Brazilian. Before his move to the Brazilian league, his injury record at AC Milan was as bad as Daniel Sturridgeai??i??s. All 4 of the Liverpool forwards have proven themselves either in the Premier League (Ings, Sturridge, Benteke) or the French Ligue 1 (Origi).

Pato is exactly the kind of transfer Liverpool need to steer clear of. Additionally, talks of an early exit from the club for Christian Benteke are ridiculous. The big Belgian has not had time to settle at the club, with his 17 appearances for the club being overseen by two different managers with different styles of playing, and both of these styles being vastly different from how he was played at Aston Villa last season. He deserves till the end of this season at the very least, if not more.

This is the a emergency signinga scenario — a situation all managers (and Boards) hope never arises. For a club with a relatively deep squad like Liverpool, injuries should be the last reason to sign a player, but there are exceptions. For example, the centre-half situation at Liverpool right now. When youai??i??re forced to play Jose Enrique and Tiago Ilori (who started his first competitive game of the season) as the centre-back pairing, the situation is truly dire. One could make a case for signing an experienced centre-half to step in, like Andrea Ranocchia (Inter Milan) and Neven Subotic (Borussia Dortmund), both of whom have been linked with a transfer to Liverpool FC.

Even in such an extreme scenario, seeing how Mamadou Sakho and Kolo Toure may possibly return within the week, these signings make no sense. You donai??i??t spend A?7 to A?10 million on players just to feature in a few games. Hopefully Liverpool FC will make it out of this window without any such expenditures.

History teaches us that short-cuts and quick-fixes can be accompanied by pretty massive pitfalls. Liverpool FC fans need to stop looking to the transfer market for the answers. Jurgen Klopp is at the helm, and his methods require investing time and effort in the players he works with. Heai??i??ll sign players when he comes across the right ones, but hopefully wonai??i??t be spending money searching for some unicorn signing that will miraculously fly the club to success.

And it is absolutely the right approach to take.

#1706. Manchester City vs Napoli - prediction, team news, lineups

By Lewis Nolan | 22 Nov 2026 16:20, Last updated: 22 Nov 2026 20:57

Manchester City will look to climb the Champions League table and restart their season by beating visitors Napoli at the Etihad on Tuesday.

The Citizens are seventh with nine points in the league phase and currently occupy one of eight automatic spots for the round of 16, whereas their Italian opponents are 27th with just three points after four gamedays.

City's woes in the Premier League continued on Saturday afternoon, when they were held to a 1-1 stalemate by Fulham, who left their hosts third in the Premier League table.

Enzo Maresca's side have now lost three and drawn one of their past four top-flight outings, while they have won four and lost four of their nine most recent matches.

One of those defeats was a 4-2 loss against Paris Saint-Germain on October 24 in their fourth Champions League clash of the season.

The hosts' defensive frailties were routinely exposed by PSG, and it should concern fans the club have conceded at least two goals in seven of their last 11 fixtures, a period in which they kept just one clean sheet.

Maresca's side have still largely succeeded at home considering they have triumphed in seven of their 10 contests at the Etihad this term, suffering two defeats in that time.

City have conceded 14 goals in their past seven clashes at the stadium, while they managed to find the back of the net on 18 occasions.

Kevin De Bruyne will return to the Etihad once again as a Napoli player, though his side have been defeated in each of their last three meetings with their English hosts.

The visitors appointed Massimiliano Allegri as the successor to Antonio Conte, who won Serie A in 2024-25, the Supercoppa Italiana in 2025-26 and guided the club to second place in May, but the current manager's spell in the dugout has been disastrous.

The visitors have won six of their 16 fixtures this campaign, and they head to the Etihad having been beaten in two of their past four games, emerging as victors once.

Gli Azzurri are eighth in the Serie A table with 18 points following their 1-0 win against Torino on Saturday, and their situation in Europe is also concerning given they have lost to Arsenal, Villarreal and Porto.

They have conceded 11 times so far in the Champions League, and though they have netted six goals, they scored just six goals in their past seven away contests in all competitions.

Napoli were beaten in five of those seven matches on the road, with their only victory a 4-1 win against Monza on October 28.

Man City know they will be without winger Antoine Semenyo, while there are also concerns about right-back Matheus Nunes.

Should both miss out, expect to see Abdukodir Khusanov on the right side of defence, with Iliman Ndiaye and Jeremy Doku on the flanks.

Midfielder Enzo Fernandez was left out of the XI against Fulham, but he will likely return in place of teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Napoli will be without defender Giovanni Di Lorenzo and the banned Rafa Marin, so perhaps Amir Rrahmani and Sam Beukema will line up in a two-man central defensive pairing.

With midfielder Stanislav Lobotka ruled out, it would not be surprising to see Frank Anguissa, Billy Gilmour and Scott McTominay stationed in the middle of the pitch.

De Bruyne could be used in an advanced role in order to alleviate him of defensive responsibilities, though he will be expected to supply striker Rasmus Hojlund.

Manchester City possible starting lineup:

Donnarumma; Khusanov, Dias, Guehi, Gvardiol; Anderson, Fernandez; Ndiaye, Cherki, Doku; Haaland

Milinkovic-Savic; Politano, Rrahmani, Beukema, Spinazzola; Anguissa, Gilmour, McTominay; De Bruyne; Hojlund, Lang

Regardless of City's poor form, it is difficult to see Napoli travelling to the Etihad and defying their record against the Citizens to claim three points.

However, the hosts have been far too open defensively, and the club's frailties at the back could lead to yet another disappointing result.

#1705. Arena aiming to make home advantage count in San Jose’s playoff opener

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Bruce Arena insisted the San Jose Earthquakes must use the PayPal Park atmosphere to their advantage in their MLS Cup Playoff opener against the Houston Dynamo.

San Jose are back in the playoffs for the first time since 2023 after a strong regular season that saw them finish fourth in the Western Conference, one point clear of Houston.

The Earthquakes have won just one of their last seven MLS games (D4 L2) and enter the postseason on the back of a 3-1 loss to Minnesota United.

And their record on home soil has not been the best in 2026. San Jose won just seven matches in front of their own supporters in the league, the fifth-lowest tally in the West.

Arena, however, believes the San Jose supporters have a big role to play when Houston visit for Game 1 of their best-of-three series.

"Making the playoffs was our goal, and we achieved that," said Arena. "Now it's going to be important to get a big crowd for the first game against Houston.

"Home-field advantage means something, so if we can get the support from the stands and play well on the field, hopefully that produces a win."

there’s nothing like a home playoff match this is what we play for. this is who we play for. the kind of atmosphere you have to experience for yourself. https://t.co/z3McgjIpfq

— San Jose Earthquakes (@SJEarthquakes) November 22, 2026

Houston, meanwhile, signed off for the playoffs with back-to-back defeats, including a Decision Day loss against St. Louis City SC, with Lukas MacNaughton netting a late winner.

But when it comes to the playoffs, the Dynamo have great pedigree. Only three teams have won back-to-back MLS Cup titles, including the 2006-07 Houston side.

The Dynamo also reached the MLS Cup final in 2011 and 2012, but were beaten by the LA Galaxy on both occasions, with the team out for revenge 15 years later.

They have already won the 2023 U.S. Open Cup under head coach Ben Olsen, and now could tie the Columbus Crew (three) for the third-most titles in league history.

Judd was the key to San Jose's offence this season, scoring 17 goals in the MLS regular season.

No Earthquakes player has scored more in a single regular season since Chris Wondolowski scored 27 in 2012.

Houston built its season on a strong defence, which can be highlighted by Halter’s tackle success rate.

Of Dynamo players who played a minimum of 1000 minutes, no player was more successful in their tackles, as he recorded a tackle success rate of 73.1%.

"A winning mentality, hungry for winning titles. To be able to make history for this club." It's the playoffs. The mentality has shifted. The energy has shifted. The focus has shifted. We're hungry for more. https://t.co/SJ7qpmS97C

— Houston Dynamo FC (@HoustonDynamo) November 21, 2026

MATCH PREDICTION: SAN JOSE EARTHQUAKES WIN

San Jose and Houston have never met in the MLS Cup playoffs but have played 37 regular-season matches, with the Dynamo leading the series with 19 wins to San Jose's 12 (six draws).

The Earthquakes are, however, currently on a four-game undefeated streak against the Dynamo (W2 D2), having not lost since 2024, setting up an intriguing encounter.

It is the first time since 2023 that San Jose have qualified for the playoffs. They have advanced past Round One only once since returning to the MLS in 2008, knocking out New York Red Bulls in 2010.

Houston, meanwhile, are making their first appearance in the playoffs since 2024, coming in with a record of W18 D11 L11 in the postseason.

Their last playoff win came against Sporting Kansas City in 2023, and they have since managed a record of W0 D2 L1.

#1704. San Jose Earthquakes vs Houston Dynamo - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 22 Nov 2026 16:28

Featuring in the playoffs for the first time since 2023, the San Jose Earthquakes will welcome the Houston Dynamo to PayPal Park on Tuesday for game one of that best-of-three series.

A 3-1 loss at Minnesota United on Decision Day meant the Quakes finished fourth in the MLS table out West, while Houston was a point behind them in fifth after a 1-0 home defeat to St Louis City.

After narrowly missing the post-season a year ago, San Jose got the job done this time around, earning 52 points, 11 more than they had in 2025.

Bruce Arena guided them to a 14-win regular season in 2026, the most for this club since 2013, when they also won 14 times.

Heading into the post-season, San Jose are on a six-match MLS unbeaten run at home, winning their last match at PayPal Park 2-1 versus Real Salt Lake on Halloween.

This year they have found the back of the net in all but two MLS affairs at home, while scoring multiple goals on nine occasions.

On Tuesday they can claim their first playoff victory since 2012 and earn their first post-season triumph at home since 2004 (2-0 over the Kansas City Wizards).

The Quakes are unbeaten in their last four MLS games against Houston, blanking them 1-0 at PayPal Park earlier this season.

After failing to make the playoffs for the first time in his tenure last year, Ben Olsen and the Dynamo bounced back with a much more consistent 2026 campaign.

During this regular season, Houston collected 51 points, 14 more than a year ago, while finishing seven places higher in the Western Conference table.

Their 43 goals scored during the regular season were the fewest among the MLS sides that made the playoffs, though they gave up the third fewest in the West (43) as well.

A win in game one would mark the first for this club away from home in the post-season since 2017, when they defeated the Timbers 2-1 in Portland.

In 2026, the Dynamo created the third-fewest big chances in MLS (66) and conceded the fourth-fewest goals per match (1.3).

San Jose Earthquakes Major League Soccer form:

San Jose will be missing DeJuan Jones as he recovers from Achilles tendon surgery, while Nonso Adimabua may not be ready to return from his lower body injury.

Preston Judd had their only strike against Minnesota the last time out, with Angus Gunn conceding three second-half goals between the sticks as he drew back into the fold over Earl Edwards Jr.

Over at Houston, Marcelo Saracchi may not be available due to a knock, and Jimmy Maurer is doubtful because of a head injury.

Guilherme will be relied upon to provide scoring for this team in the playoffs, with the Brazilian leading them with 16 goals in the regular season, along with 10 assists, while Mateusz Bogusz was second with eight goals.

San Jose Earthquakes possible starting lineup:

Gunn; Kikanovic, Munie, Romney, Ricketts; Vieira, Lowen; Harkes, Tsakiris, Werner; Judd

Bond; Ennali, Andrade, Resch, Halter, Negri; Herrera, Artur, Bogusz; Foster, Guilherme

The Quakes play with much more aggression and on the front foot at home, and we believe they have enough creativity to find a way through a strong Dynamo backline that could be defending for long stretches in game one.

#1703. Opposition insight for Milan-Frosinone: Form, injuries, predicted XI and more

AC Milan are looking to make it three consecutive wins tomorrow, but a high-flying newcomer in Frosinone could make that difficult.

Ruben Amorim and his men have an opportunity to really establish some momentum tomorrow evening, picking up where they left off before the break. However, it won’t be an easy game against Massimiliano Alvani’s Frosinone, who have impressed everyone so far.

Amorim even warned in his press conference that it will be a difficult one, especially since the Canarini have such a direct style.

➤ Manager: Massimiliano Alvini ➤ Form (all comps): W-D-W-W-L (most recent) ➤ Top scorer (Serie A): Raimondo – 8 ➤ Most assists (Serie A): Kvernadze, Schmid and Ghedjemis – 4 ➤ Injuries & suspensions: Bracaglia, Grillitsch and Raimondo.

Frosinone have definitely been one of the surprises of the season so far. After a very strong Serie B campaign with 81 points and only three games lost, they secured direct promotion to the top tier (finishing second) and have been making the most of the adventure.

They are currently on 20 points after eleven games, winning six, drawing two and losing three, which has put them in sixth place. That’s very strong for a newcomer and for a coach who is only in his second season with the club, especially considering the upset against Como.

It’s the 56-year-old’s second attempt at Serie A after coaching Cremonese for half a season in 2022-23. He didn’t manage a single win then, so you can definitely say that the performance so far has been great revenge for him.

So, what is behind this rise? As highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport this morning, the direct style of play has been key for Frosinone. As opposed to Milan, who want to see a lot of the ball, they are willing to have less possession and break on the counter.

It doesn’t mean that they sit back, though. In fact, it has been the opposite as they are the highest-pressing team in the league. The strategy thus seems to be to force mistakes out of the opponents, while also making sure that they are direct in possession.

While collective effort deserves most of the praise, it has definitely helped that the likes of Giacomo Calo, Giorgi Kvernadze and Antonio Raimondo – among others – have performed at a very high level. They aren’t exactly big-name players, so a lot of them are having their breakout seasons.

Moving on to actual team news, the situation up front is not ideal for Frosinone as their top scorer, the aforementioned Antonio Raimondo, is out injured. Birigilea, who is on two goals, is set to replace him in the No.9 position.

The Milan academy product Sebastiano Desplanches, who left the club four years ago, will be on the bench. He’s yet to make an appearance this season, with Alvini preferring Lorenzo Palmisani instead.

Predicted Frosinone XI (4-2-3-1): Palmisani; Oyono, Calvani, Monterisi, Terzic; Calo, Masini; Ghedjemis; Schmid, Kvernadze; Birigilea.

Predicted bench: Desplanches, Pisseri, Cittadini, Tchato, Amey, Akpoguma, Fayed, El Azzouzi, Cichella, Hasa, Fini, Zerbin, Bobcek.

#1702. Liverpool vs Arsenal Preview: Team News, Tactics, Lineups and Prediction

Home » Home 2 » Liverpool vs Arsenal Preview: Team News, Tactics, Lineups and Prediction

Table-toppers Arsenal travel to Anfield tonight with their first Premier League trophy since the ‘invincibles’ season of 2004 in sight. The Gunners top the table and with stuttering performances from Manchester City and a Leicester City whose fairytale run seems at an end, and are in pole position to finish the current campaign as champions.

While Jurgen Klopp’s men are still finding their way inconsistently since his appointment, Arsenal are in top form with five victories out of their last six matches. In comparison, Liverpool have been as easy to predict as a magic 8 ball, with impressive wins over Leicester City and Manchester City, but accompanied with horrific losses against Watford and West Ham. With fourth place still within grasp and with an impressive record against the table topping teams this season, Liverpool would look to give their long suffering fans some cheer with which to greet this New Year.

The Reds desperately need a victory to steady the ship as their erratic and wayward form sees them enter 2016 still outside the top 4 and distant from any title challenge.

With a host of injuries to his main XI, Jurgen Klopp could be forgiven for dipping into the transfer market so early. The Reds have captured QPR right-back Steven Caulker along with Marko Grujic in the January transfer window.

With Grujic returning to his former club Red Star Belgrade on loan, Steven Caulker is likely to be given a run out as a substitute with the current spate of Liverpool injuries.

Ings, Sturridge, Lovren, Coutinho, Origi and Flanagan are amongst the Liverpool afflicted and will take no part in the match ahead. With Lovren out, Kolo Toure and Mamadou Sakho look likely to be Klopp’s first choice central defending partnership.

Alberto Moreno and Nathaniel Clyne should start as full-backs for the Liverpool side and will be crucial in any attempt to penetrate the Gunner’s defences. Emre Can and Lucas should marshal the midfield, while James Milner, Firmino and Adam Lallana look to give Petr Cech some concerns about his goal. Leading the line should be Christian Benteke, who’s lack of form doesn’t threaten this match as manager Klopp has few options in his position.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Mignolet; Clyne, Sakho, Toure, Moreno; Lucas, Can, Firmino, Lallana, Milner, Benteke.

Arsenal must show that they have the one quality required of all champions : Consistency. The task is hereby straightforward for Wenger’s men. Win, keep winning, regardless of your manner and the title is yours.

With half the season concluded, Arsene Wenger must be wishing that he received a Christmas gift from the Arsenal medical team. Injuries have decimated his midfield with Wilshire, Cazorla, Rosiscky, Coquelin and Sanchez out of the game.

There is some good news with Mesul Ozil having managed to partake in some leisure instead of participating in the FA cup victory over Sunderland. Keeping the nimble playmaker fit would be key to Arsenal aspirations, both in this match and for the remainder of the season.

With both Petr Mertersacker and Gabriel available, it would be interesting to see whom Arsene Wenger picks out for his starting XI. Koscielny, Bellerin and Monreal have nailed down their place in the defence and the inclusion of the slower Mertersacker or the inconsistent Gabriel may have a defining moment in the game.

With Arsenal’s midfield woes, it should fall to Flamini to screen the defence with Ramsey alongside him. Walcott, Ozil and Joel Campbell should be the main thrusts of Arsenal’s attacking play with Giroud as the elegant, decisive focus.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Cech; Bellerin, Gabriel, Koscielny, Monreal; Flamini, Ramsey, Ozil, Walcott, Campbell; Girourd.

With previous encounters between these teams resulting in high scoring draws, we favour a repeat of last year’s epic 2-2 result for the same fixture. Martin Skrtel’s 97th minute header in front of the Kop capped a memorable game which also had Fabio Borini sent off and we expect similar fireworks at Anfield tomorrow.

#1701. Andrews’ ‘ambitious’ changes pay off in Brentford’s thrashing of Everton

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Keith Andrews said his decision to make several changes to Brentford's starting line-up against Everton on Monday showed ambition to compete on all fronts this season.

Andrews watched on as his Brentford side responded from their 2-0 defeat to Brighton ahead of the international break with a thumping 4-0 triumph over 10-man Everton.

Keane Lewis-Potter netted twice in the space of 178 seconds in the first half to put the Bees in control before Everton captain James Tarkowski was sent off in the 40th minute.

Tarkowski was dismissed for catching Yehor Yarmoliuk high on his shin after clearing the ball, with referee Craig Pawson overruling his original decision after a VAR review.

Vitaly Janelt's 67th-minute thunderbolt was the pick of Brentford's goals, with substitute Fabio Carvalho climbing off the bench to add further gloss to the scoreline late on.

Brentford enjoyed their joint-biggest home win in the Premier League, equalling their 4-0 rout of Manchester United in August 2022, with their display coming after Andrews elected to make four changes to the side that were beaten by Brighton.

Callum Wilson replaced the suspended Igor Thiago up front, while Yarmoliuk, Mikkel Damsgaard and Jaidon Anthony all came in to replace Mamadou Sangare and Kevin Schade, while Aaron Hickey missed out all together through injury.

"Big impact, it's the nature of the game and the squad. We have the luxury of choosing from very good players," Andrews told Sky Sports on the reason behind his alterations.

"Some will be disappointed not to play more, but the reality is we need everybody. We want to be ambitious, so we need everybody. The boys that came in did really well."

After missing out on European football last season, Brentford's win saw them climb up to sixth in the Premier League and just four points adrift of fourth-place Liverpool.

"We know what the other side feels like, but I wanted to keep our habits, be professional, try to control the game and wait for the right openings," Andrews added.

"Each game is very different, very difficult. The expectation levels at this club have changed and, regardless of the performance, the win to go sixth in the league and still questions about 'should they be doing better?' – I think people need to get real.

"I'm really happy with the group, the club and long may it continue. Long way to go. Onto Old Trafford on Saturday and we're really looking forward to it."

Since Andrews took charge of Brentford ahead of the 2025-26 season, of London clubs, only Arsenal (113) have won more Premier League points than the Bees (70).

Brentford also hit the 300-goal mark in the Premier League in their 201st game in the competition (303 goals in total), the fifth-fastest side to do so, after Man United (165), Newcastle United (170), Liverpool (190) and Blackburn Rovers (191).

Lewis-Potter got the landmark goal, and in 11 appearances this season, he has already beaten his best-ever scoring season in the Premier League (three in 36 apps in 2025-26 and 3 in 30 in 2023-24), with his double taking him to four this term.

"He's been excellent, growing all the time since I've been here," Andrews said of Lewis-Potter.

"Finds himself in unnatural positions – we give him the freedom to go and roam, and he's proving very difficult for the opposition to mark."

#1700. Cherki magic helping Maresca to step out of Guardiola shadow

Rumours of Manchester City’s supposed demise without Pep Guardiola appear to be much exaggerated.

They swept past Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park with a style of play under new manager Enzo Maresca that was just as swashbuckling as under his predecessor, with Rayan Cherki playing the role of chief architect. The Frenchman’s two goals included a captivating mazy dribble, which will long be remembered by those who had the fortune to see it.

City created enough space for themselves through clever movement. With Cherki zigging one way and Phil Foden zagging the other, they created even more by dribbling past a mesmerised Palace back three that became a back five at times and still could not cope.

Erling Haaland also scored twice. Even with the creative and unpredictable talents of those behind in a four-man attacking City midfield, Haaland remains irreplaceable with his ability to convert chances.

However, this night belonged to Cherki. Guardiola chided him publicly after he set up a City goal with a “rabona” cross last season. The thrust of Guardiola’s comments were that Cherki was not Lionel Messi. Of course not, but he possesses a genius all of his own, which Maresca would surely be foolish to rein in.

The jaw-dropping splendour of Cherki’s first goal drew a collective intake of breath at Selhurst Park.

Collecting a Foden pass, he attacked the Palace area on a diagonal path, slaloming between Jaydee Canvot, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chris Richards, before having the spatial awareness and technique to flick his left foot at the ball to send it rolling on a perpendicular trajectory past Dean Henderson.

"The man with the magic feet!"Rayan Cherki doubles Manchester City's lead with a STUNNING goal 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/9Zea5vFljv

An insight into Cherki’s mindset came after the match.

He said: “My performance is s---. In the first half, we didn’t find the space, I played bad. I need to show them that I want to play, I want to score. Next time I want to give the ball around more.”

Forget the words, Maresca cannot ignore the actions of a player he left on the bench against Bournemouth.

Sterner tests will come for City than against a Palace side missing key players who may or may not leave south London in the remaining days of the transfer window.

Whether Maresca will trust his forward players to express themselves as freely against their rivals for the Premier League title remains to be seen, but with Elliot Anderson providing a one-man shield behind them, City could not be stopped.

Maresca said: “For sure Rayan is happy tonight. His performance was very good and not just for his two goals. He has to press off the ball and he was in charge of [marking] Adam Wharton, so it was a complete game by him.”

Only for the first three minutes did Palace hint at a different outcome but, after shots from Eddie Nketiah and Daichi Kamada were diverted away for corners, City took control.

They took the lead in the 17th minute when the otherwise quiet Antoine Semenyo flighted a cross over the heads of everyone except the shorn locks of Haaland, whose determined header looped over Henderson and dropped in the far corner.

The only negative of Foden’s performance came in front of goal, with a ballooned shot and a mistimed header.

After Cherki’s solo masterpiece had made it 2-0, Yeremy Pino seized the next moment for his own with a stunning free-kick that flicked the crossbar, then the back of City keeper Gianluigi Donnarumma before finally dropping over the line.

"This is a good a free-kick as you're likely to see this season!" Yéremy Pino's stirke beats Donnarumma 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5uF4vzOXDp

Whatever hope that mustered was snatched away again when Cherki scored his second goal and the third goal of a breathless five minutes.

His shot at the end of a darting run flicked the ankle of Tomiyasu to send it just out of Henderson’s reach.

Rayan Cherki AGAIN! Manchester City have breathing room once again after another strike from the Frenchman 👏 pic.twitter.com/Tyw9whPS2r

Morocco teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi had little time to show why City have paid Lille £85.6m for him with a late entry as a substitute, but they didn’t need him on this occasion.

Foden then set off on a swerving run that set up Haaland to lash home his second goal of the game and make it 4-1.

Erling Haaland scores gets another! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/4mz2eF7wFF

The fear for Palace is that they cannot keep selling their best players and expecting to replicate the success on the pitch that has brought them three trophies in the past 15 months.

Leicester City offer a shuddering example of that. From Premier League champions to League One in 10 seasons.

Pierre Sage, the new Palace manager, will welcome the certainty that the closure of the transfer window will bring, particularly over the futures of forwards Ismaïla Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta, as well as wing-back Daniel Muñoz.

The one player he cannot afford to lose is Wharton, who matched the City midfield on his own at times in the first half.

Sage said: “I think the score is heavy. We stayed in the game for 65 minutes and created some chances. We know we are in for a tough season, but we have created a lot of opportunities in the first two games.

“I could speak about the transfer window, but I don’t want to find an excuse. We just have to be sure that in four days’ time, the team will be better than today.”

“It has been a short pre-season. Rayan [Cherki], five weeks ago was at the World Cup. Game by game, we will be back, just need a few games. We played well, it is a new manager but we have been playing together, with the addition of a few new players. We know what to do and have to trust the system.”

“We have to keep on playing together, find out where we are best and how to play. We have so many good players and we have to fit everyone in. He has to keep going because we know how good Phil is, it is about showing it week in week out. This is the right step forward for everyone. We have to build on this.”

"I'm just trying to play my football" 💪Elliot Anderson is excited about the future at Manchester City after his summer transfer 🔥 pic.twitter.com/huGv4Li3GZ

"Say what you actually mean!" 🤣Erling Haaland takes over Rayan Cherki's post-match interview! pic.twitter.com/adW6IU8DzQ

2 + 2 - Rayan Cherki is the third player to have a game with multiple goals and another game with multiple assists across a team's first two matches of a Premier League campaign, after Thierry Henry in 2004-05 and Didier Drogba in 2010-11.Polymath. pic.twitter.com/4cRV0xMIFa

Pierre Sage’s side will host Middlesbrough in the League Cup third round next month and will also begin their Europa League campaign in September.

The directions of these teams will be diverging this season. City were wonderful, free-flowing, expressive and fun to watch. Palace not so much. It will take Pierre Sage a while to impose his style of play. It will certainly take another week before he knows his final squad for the first half of the season.

It was noticeable at the final whistle that many Palace fans stayed around to applaud Daniel Munoz, an unused substitute on the night, as he made his way to the tunnel, probably for the final time as a Palace player if Nottingham Forest’s interest in him becomes a transfer by the end of the window.

"Cherki was the difference" 🪄"He is a genius" 🧠Jamie Redknapp reacts to Crystal Palace 1-4 Man City 🔊 pic.twitter.com/UjSarMngDR

Possession: Crystal Palace 28%-72% Manchester CityShots: 9-18Shots on target: 1-9Corners: 2-6Touches in the opposition box: 13-33

Pretty comprehensive in Manchester City’s favour, which is reflected in the scoreline.

The final whistle is blown at Selhurst Park and Manchester City have cruised to a 4-1 win thanks to doubles from Cherki and Haaland. Enzo Maresca’s side make it two wins from two whereas it is two defeats from two for Pierre Sage.

Manchester City, with the three points already in the bag, are just stroking the ball around with ease and are in complete control. Palace can barely get a foot on it.

A late double substitution for Manchester City as Reis and Braithwaite come on. Enzo Maresca’s side are cruising to victory to make it two wins from two.

Cherki has two goals to his name and now Haaland does as Manchester City are romping to victory in south London. Guehi wins possession for City inside the Palace half and the ball comes to Foden, who dribbles towards the Palace penalty area. He lays it off to his left to Haaland who, from a narrow angle, finds the root of the net.

Erling Haaland scores gets another! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/4mz2eF7wFF

Nearly an instant impact from McAidoo as the 18-year-old drives through the Palace half and curls a shot from the edge of the box that goes just wide.

When Manchester City were making those substitutions, the Crystal Palace fans were making sure they let the officials know how long the Manchester City players were taking to get off.

There is going to be a debut for the Premier League’s most expensive teenager ever as Bouaddi comes on for Manchester City. McAidoo is also coming on, with Cherki and Anderson going off.

Mingueza eventually comes on but not after having to wait until the ball goes out of play again as Khalaili was adjudged to have taken too long to have got off the pitch. Safe to say the Palace fans are not too impressed with that new rule. It will probably be a pub question in the years ahead. That change does mean that Palace have used all five substitutions, which means Munoz will not come on. He is being linked with a reunion with Oliver Glasner at Nottingham Forest in the final days of this window.

Crystal Palace make another double change and it will be two debuts as Disasi and Mingueza come on.

Enzo Maresca turns to his bench for the first time tonight as Kovacic comes on.

Khalaili brings down Semenyo and is booked for that challenge.

Palace are going to make a double substitution as McNeil and Gozo replace Nketiah and Pino. 19-year-old Gozo is on for his Palace debut.

That was a chance for Palace. Guessand finds Pino, who drives into the Manchester City penalty area on the right. Pino has Nketiah at the far post but there is too much on the cross.

Guessand, back at Palace, is going to come on to replace Strand Larsen, who has been pretty quiet up top for the home side tonight.

Sometimes you feel blessed to witness an extraordinary moment of footballing genius. Selhurst Park has just seen two in the space of three minutes. Yeremy Pino’s free-kick which flicked off the back of Gianluigi Donnarumma was stunning, but even that could not truly compare to the slalom run of Rayan Cherki that drew a collective intake of breath from all those present. The Frenchman has just followed it with a scorching shot. It couldn’t compare with his first, though.

Three goals come in quick succession and Cherki restores Manchester City’s two-goal advantage with his second of the night. The Frenchman receives it on the turn from around 30 yards out and drives towards the Palace penalty area. He then shoots and a kind deflection off Richards takes it over Henderson’s diving effort and into the Palace net.

Rayan Cherki AGAIN! Manchester City have breathing room once again after another strike from the Frenchman 👏 pic.twitter.com/Tyw9whPS2r

Just as the hosts appeared to maybe out of this one, they get a goal back. Pino’s fantastic free-kick strikes the bar, hits Donnarumma on the back before going into the net off the post. That hit the frame of the goal twice and Palace have a crucial goal, minutes after going 2-0 down.

"This is a good a free-kick as you're likely to see this season!" Yéremy Pino's stirke beats Donnarumma 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5uF4vzOXDp

Anderson brings down Pino not far outside the Manchester City penalty area and is booked.

The next goal in this game felt crucial and the visitors have it. Foden drives towards the Palace penalty area before playing a pass forward into the path of Cherki. The Frenchman has numerous defenders around but he shows neat footwork to skip past a few, holds off Richards before slotting home with his left foot.

"The man with the magic feet!"Rayan Cherki doubles Manchester City's lead with a STUNNING goal 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/9Zea5vFljv

No-one has had fewer touches on the pitch tonight than Haaland up until this point but the Norwegian’s goal is the difference. His number of touches (14) is the joint fewest with his compatriot Strand Larsen.

That was a good chance for Nketiah. He plays the ball to the underlapping Mitchell, who from the byline cuts it back into the path of Nketiah. The former Arsenal man should so so much better with his opportunity from the edge of the six-yard box but fires a long way wide.

Semenyo wins Manchester City an early corner in this second half off Canvot. Anderson’s delivery beyond the back post picks out O’Reilly, who in space heads back across goal but Pino heads away.

We are back under way at Selhurst Park, with Manchester City carrying a 1-0 lead into this second half. As the players emerged from the tunnels for the second half, the DJ at Selhurst Park paid tribute to the late Dolly Parton and Kenny Rogers by playing Islands in the Stream. Nice touch! Get your favourite Dolly and Kenny tunes in the comments section at the bottom of the blog.

Possession: Crystal Palace 33%-67% Manchester CityShots: 7-11Shots on target: 1-6Corners: 2-2Touches in the opposition box: 10-18

The stats are certainly in Manchester City’s favour and they will feel they probably should have more than the one goal.

Cherki has a late chance for Manchester City but his shot is well saved by Henderson down to his right.

The first half at Selhurst Park is then brought to an end and Manchester City lead 1-0 at the break thanks to Haaland’s header.

There will be just one added minute at the end of this first half.

Palace started off with a nominal back three. That has become a back five far too often for Pierre Sage’s liking at times in this first half, yet still City are playing through them almost at will. The Palace fans whose deafening support accompanied Palace shots in the opening minutes are reduced to cheering battling midfield runs that win a free-kick now.

Pino delivers a free-kick into the Manchester City box and Richards gets to it first. It comes off his shoulder and rolls into the arms of Donnarumma.

Semenyo’s shot from the left side of the box takes a deflection off Richards, forcing Henderson into a decent save.

Palace now miss a big opportunity and should be on level terms. Wharton, who has probably been the best player on the pitch tonight, whips in a cross from the right and picks out Mitchell, who has a free header from eight yards out but somehow misses the target.

Strand Larsen comes close with a header from a Pino cross but he would have been offside anyway.

The first booking of the night goes the way of the visitors. Wharton drives forward into the Manchester City half and is cynically brought down by Cherki, who looked perplexed when the yellow card was shown but it was an obvious booking.

Foden wastes his second big chance of this first half. Manchester City break through O’Reilly, who carries it down the right. He waits for Cherki to make the overlapping run before passing to the Frenchman. Cherki’s cross picks out Foden inside the six-yard box and the latter should score but he gets a simple header all wrong.

Well, that was easy. So easy in fact – perfect Semenyo cross, perfect Haaland header - that it hushed Selhurst Park as the ball looped over Dean Henderson. Even the roar from the enclave of City fans took a moment to fill the south London air. You wouldn’t say that all the pre-match optimism among Palace fans has been punctured, but the home side need a moment if they aren’t to sink without trace to a City side bossing possession and territory now.

That is a huge miss from Foden. Anderson picks out his compatriot in acres of space on the right side of the box, with no Palace defender within five yards of him, but Foden blazes over the bar when he should have put Manchester City 2-0 up.

King Harald V of Norway has died in the last few days and over the last few hours two Norwegian cyclists claimed a one-two at the Vuelta a Espana and now Haaland has a goal.

He has barely touched the ball thus far but he puts the visitors ahead just past the quarter-of-an-hour mark. Semenyo is afforded too much space on the left just outside the penalty area and clips in a cross towards the far post. Haaland gets up highest, above Richards, and guides a superb header over Henderson into the Palace net.

Erling Haaland gets off the mark for the new Premier League season! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/5ZjQUVk6Zl

The England boss is in attendance tonight, perhaps keeping a close eye on that midfield battle between Anderson and Wharton.

Palace flirt with danger inside their own penalty area. After Haaland’s flick, Kamada should just belt the ball away but instead inexplicably leaves it. Henderson manages to mop up just as Foden was eyeing up the chance.

There is a mad scramble inside the Palace box but somehow the hosts escape without conceding. Initially, Anderson’s shot from range is saved by Henderson but Manchester City keep it alive in the penalty area. Palace frantically attempt to clear their lines and eventually they do after Haaland came close.

Quite a lot of the focus tonight will be on two English midfielders; one who has got a big-money move this summer and the other thus far has not. Anderson is directly up against Wharton and so far it is the latter who is winning the early battles, including dispossessing Anderson in midfield.

The first chance of the game goes the way of the hosts. It stems from a quite sensational first-time pass from Wharton from inside his own half into the left channel to pick out the run of Nketiah, whose shot from the left side of the box takes a deflection off Dias and is saved by Donnarumma.

Manchester City initially clear the corner but Palace keep it alive. Kamada’s shot from just inside the box appeared to be on target but it is headed over for another corner, which is easily caught by Donnarumma.

We are under way at Selhurst Park. Will Pierre Sage earn his first win as Palace boss or can Enzo Maresca and City make it two wins from two?

Both sides emerge from the tunnel in the corner of Selhurst Park to the customary sound of Glad All Over and we are moments away from kick-off in south London. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

Crystal Palace: Henderson, Khalaili, Canvot, Richards, Tomiyasu, Mitchell, Wharton, Kamada, Pino, Strand Larsen, Nketiah.Substitutes: Benitez, Munoz, Disasi, Mingueza, Hughes, Lerma, Gozo, McNeil, Guessand.

Manchester City: Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias, Gvardiol, O’Reilly, Anderson, Guehi, Cherki, Foden Semenyo, Haaland.Substitutes: Rulli, Kovacic, Ait-Nouri, Reis, Echeverri, Bouaddi, McAidoo, Braithwaite, Lewis.

Yes! It may have been fleeting but the boy in the Palace tracksuit top had his moment after all with Erling Haaland as City waited in line to enter the Selhurst Park pitch. And having done so, he fairly skipped up the steps back with his dad back to their seats. Whether the boy’s second wish of the evening, for a Palace victory, will come true is another question altogether.

The young Palace fan is still waiting for Haaland. Another determined walk back to the dressing room. It isn’t a simple task to attract an opposition player’s attention when you are leaning over a barrier a few feet higher than him – and in the home end. Haaland and his teammates have the look of a team that knows it must perform tonight to ease the concerns that they are a team in transition. The City fans will not entertain such thoughts, either.

Crystal Palace looked set to sign Club Brugge defender Joel Ordonez but that deal could be in doubt as there may be some problems with his medical. We await to see further updates on that situation.

“He is a genius. Make no mistake. Managers now want structure, they do not like players who are a bit loose out of possession. But I go to football matches to watch people like him play.

“That is what makes me smile. I do not like watching players pass it sideways, that is not why I go to football. I go to watch geniuses do their work. Some managers will not appreciate it. But last week he got his manager out of a hole because without him they would not have won that game.”

"He's irreplaceable" 💥Jamie Redknapp and Clinton Morrison sing the praises of Crystal Palace's Adam Wharton 🤝 pic.twitter.com/ZOpcZcItHY

Jack Grealish is not in the Manchester City squad tonight amid links with the likes of Everton and Sunderland. Will he still be at the club beyond the deadline? It would appear not.

Both Ismaila Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta are out of the Crystal Palace squad tonight with injury but could they be on the move before the window slams shut? Sarr has been linked with Galatasaray and Liverpool whilst the situation is complicated with Mateta as he claims the final year of his contract is void. How do those two situations resolve themselves? Daniel Munoz has been linked with a move to Nottingham Forest but is on the bench for Palace this evening.

An unfulfilled wish so far for a young Palace fan holding up a child’s red Norway shirt with ‘Haaland’ emblazoned on it. Having waited patiently for the City players to emerge for their warm-up and being held by his dad as he leant over the stone wall to attract Haaland’s attention, he was left disappointed because the City striker was simply not looking as he and his teammates jogged past. Will the boy, who has on a Palace tracksuit top, get a photo with his hero when the striker returns to the Portakabin that hosts the away dressing room prior to kick-off? Stay tuned.

"The results will certainly come" ✅Dean Henderson urges patience as Crystal Palace go through a transitional period under new manager Pierre Sage 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/1pJjRPeKko

"On the ball I think he's very good, off the ball he's strong" Enzo Maresca explains why he played Marc Guéhi in midfield in Manchester City's opening game against Bournemouth 🤔 pic.twitter.com/h4N1e1L8bf

"At home anything is possible" 💪Pierre Sage previews his sides clash with Manchester City at Selhurst Park 🔥 pic.twitter.com/oPJnZJVB6B

"He'll be very vital for us" 🔑Nico O'Reilly speaking about Manchester City's new signing Ayyoub Bouaddi ahead of their game against Crystal Palace 🔊 pic.twitter.com/2ptihsCY7c

Anan Khalaili and Takehiro Tomiyasu make their first starts for the hosts tonight and there could be a debut off the bench for Axel Disasi, who joined on loan from Chelsea.

Crystal Palace: Henderson, Khalaili, Canvot, Richards, Tomiyasu, Mitchell, Wharton, Kamada, Pino, Strand Larsen, Nketiah.Substitutes: Benitez, Munoz, Disasi, Mingueza, Hughes, Lerma, Gozo, McNeil, Guessand.

There looks set to be a debut for the Premier League’s most expensive teenager off the visitors’ bench in the form of Ayyoub Bouaddi. There is no Jack Grealish in their squad as his future is up in the air.

Manchester City: Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias, Gvardiol, O’Reilly, Anderson, Guehi, Cherki, Foden Semenyo, Haaland.Substitutes: Rulli, Kovacic, Ait-Nouri, Reis, Echeverri, Bouaddi, McAidoo, Braithwaite, Lewis.

Was it really just a year ago when Crystal Palace fans flooded down the Holmesdale Road with not a care in the world having just won the Community Shield to add to their FA Cup triumph over tonight’s opponents Manchester City? Well, they are marching along the Holmesdale Road in the same numbers again this evening, bedecked in red and blue as always, yet there is uncertainty and worry in the air and on their faces. Will the player exodus continue? What should they make of new manager Pierre Sage? Will the good times fade from view as quickly as they did for Leicester City or can Sage build a new side to match the one which, under Oliver Glasner, added the Conference League to their list of trophies three months ago?

“We struggled to get into the game and win the battles,” a disappointed Carlo Ancelotti lamented.

At the World Cup, an industrious 18-year-old showed maturity beyond his years to dominate the midfield against Ancelotti’s Brazil on his competitive international debut, earning Morocco a draw. That was, in fact, the second time an Ancelotti side had been undone by precocious teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Ancelotti’s remarks about losing the midfield battle are from after a Champions League match in October 2024, when Lille shocked Real Madrid to end their 36-game unbeaten run. Bouaddi was at the heart of both statement results for his club and country.

The second weekend of the Premier League season kicks off under the lights in South London as Crystal Palace host Manchester City at Selhurst Park. Manchester City won both fixtures 3-0 last season and they are in fact unbeaten in their last 11 Premier league away games against Crystal Palace, who have won just two of the 22 top flight meetings.

Crystal Palace experienced defeat on the opening weekend, falling to a 2-0 loss at Everton last Saturday, meaning the Pierre Sage era started with a defeat. Tonight is Sage’s first home game in charge of the club.

“I think it will be a wonderful moment, but I prefer to have a wonderful moment with good news at the end of the game,” Sage said. “That is why I do not think about me in this situation. The most important thing is the team and the result for sure, because we prepare all the week for that, to make them [the fans] happy. They will be happy to see us, but I think they would prefer to see us win. I will give my life to make them happy. I cannot do more. When you are in this stadium [Selhurst Park], you feel the history. You feel that there is something heavy weighing on you. It is a great responsibility that I have been entrusted with. We cannot wait to see this stadium in action.”

Sage has confirmed that Ismaila Sarr, who has been linked with a move away from the club this summer, and Chadi Riad will miss out tonight due to injury, as will striker Jean-Philippe Mateta. Palace have confirmed the addition of Axel Disasi on loan from Chelsea and the French defender could be involved tonight.

Manchester City appeared to be heading towards defeat in Enzo Maresca’s first league game in charge of the club last weekend. They were 1-0 down at home against Bournemouth in the closing stages before goals from Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol gave them a come-from-behind win.

It has been a busy week in the transfer window for Manchester City. Both Savio (formerly Savinho) and Omar Marmoush have left for Tottenham, joining a long list of departures from the Etihad this summer. Moroccan midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi has arrived in an £85m deal from Lille and has become the most expensive teenager in Premier League history. Maresca has confirmed that 18-year-old Bouaddi is ready to start.

“He [Bouaddi] is ready,” Maresca said. “He was working with his former club so he is fit. We will see how long he needs in terms of adaptation but he is ready to go. He is quite calm. Bayern Munich have been linked with Roma striker Donyell Malen after Harry Kane suffered a long-term ankle injury, with Paris Saint-Germain also reportedly keen. Kane, 33, will be out for several months, a blow that could push Bayern to sign a goalscorer in the January transfer window.

Kane was injured on Friday night in the 1-1 draw with Cologne on the 10th Bundesliga matchday, and he has suffered a torn syndesmotic ligament. He must undergo surgery and will miss several months of competition. It is a major blow for boss Vincent Kompany, who has no other specialist number nine with the same status in his squad.

Given the fixtures ahead, the Champions League above all, the Bundesliga giants could use the winter window to act. Top Mercato reported that the injury could make Marseille fear a Bayern move for Amine Gouiri, but he is not the only forward who could interest the Allianz Arena club.

According to Calciomercato, Bayern are expected to position themselves for Malen, the prolific Netherlands striker. The Italian outlet says the 27-year-old ‘deserves the attention’ of the Bavarian hierarchy. Bayern have not made an offer, and signing him in the coming weeks looks very complicated given his outstanding 2026-27 season with Roma.

Malen has scored 16 goals in 15 matches in all competitions. The former Borussia Dortmund player leads the Serie A scoring charts with 12 goals in 11 appearances. On Saturday he scored four goals in Roma’s 5-1 win at Parma. His xG of 9.71, higher than Kane’s, confirms that the number 14 is overperforming.

The statistics may impress several clubs more prestigious than Roma, but Bayern have no chance of convincing the Italian club to release their number one attacking weapon in the middle of the season. Malen is under contract until June 2030, with a market value of £47m, and will not be sold before the summer of 2027.

That should also cool PSG’s interest. Faced with injuries to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue, the French capital club could see boss Luis Enrique ‘ask president Al-Khelaifi to return to the market, and asking for a top-level player like Malen is not heresy’, according to the report. Like Bayern, however, PSG will almost certainly meet a categorical refusal from Roma, at least in January.

#1696. Feyenoord vs Porto - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 22 Nov 2026 18:17

Feyenoord will be desperate to end a six-match winless run when they welcome Porto to De Kuip for Tuesday's Champions League league-phase encounter.

Both sides have collected just three points from their opening four European fixtures, leaving the Portuguese visitors 26th in the 36-team table and their Dutch hosts languishing in 32nd.

Feyenoord head into Tuesday's encounter after suffering three consecutive defeats, the latest of which came at De Kuip on Saturday when they were beaten 3-2 by Excelsior, who secured their first league victory at the ground in 46 years.

The hosts made a bright start by taking the lead through Givairo Read barely two minutes into the contest, but three goals in succession left Jan Plug's own goal little more than a consolation as De Stadionclub slipped to fifth in the Eredivisie table.

More concerning for Giovanni van Bronckhorst is his side's defensive record, having conceded at least three goals in each of their last three outings across all competitions, with Saturday's setback following a 5-3 defeat at Heerenveen and a 3-0 home loss to Inter Milan on matchday four of the Champions League league phase.

That continental defeat was the 10th in Feyenoord's last 13 European matches, while it also extended an unwanted run that has seen them concede the opening goal in each of their last seven Champions League outings, including defeats to Barcelona and Real Betis as well as their victory over Como on matchday two.

With the prospect of another early European exit looming, the Dutch club know that another setback on Tuesday would leave their hopes of reaching the knockout rounds hanging by a thread, having already fallen short in last season's Europa League league phase, where they finished 29th.

However, the hosts face a difficult examination against a Porto side who finally got their Champions League campaign up and running with an emphatic 4-1 victory over Napoli at the Estadio do Dragao on matchday four.

Francesco Farioli's men had suffered defeats to Manchester City, Real Betis and PSV in their opening three league-phase fixtures, but goals from Jan Bednarek, Gabri Veiga, Jakub Kiwior and Samu Omorodion inspired a convincing response against the Italian outfit.

That being said, Porto have won each of their opening 11 league matches this term to establish a five-point gap atop the Primeira Liga table, though the Dragons were made to work harder in Friday's Taca de Portugal encounter with third-tier Paredes, eventually progressing on penalties after a 1-1 draw across 120 minutes.

Back on the continental stage, the Dragons, featuring in the Champions League main stage for the first time in three years, will continue their quest to reach the knockout rounds for the third consecutive appearance, having progressed to the last 16 in their previous two campaigns.

Nevertheless, the visitors have not always enjoyed travelling to the Netherlands, failing to win any of their last four away matches against Dutch opposition (D2, L2), including  both previous visits to Feyenoord, having drawn at De Kuip in the Champions League in 1993 before suffering a 2-0 defeat there in 2019, while both of Porto’s victories in this fixture have come on home soil.

Feyenoord are monitoring the fitness of Anis Hadj Moussa, who returned from international duty with an ankle injury and missed Saturday's defeat to Excelsior.

Tsuyoshi Watanabe is also doubtful after being withdrawn at half time against Excelsior, with Van Bronckhorst indicating that the defender was struggling with a foot problem, while Jakub Moder and Bart Nieuwkoop remain sidelined with injuries.

Thomas Beelen (leg), Jordan Bos (ACL) and Jerry St. Juste (shin) are expected to remain unavailable, leaving the hosts with limited defensive options.

Former Arsenal winger Reiss Nelson made his first start for Feyenoord at the weekend, although Luciano Valente could be preferred on the left flank of attack against Porto.

As for the visitors, long-term absentee Vasco Sousa remains sidelined with a leg injury, while William Gomes has recovered from an ankle injury and returned to full training, although his involvement on Tuesday remains uncertain.

Former Manchester United defender Chris Smalling is also dealing with a right knee problem and is ineligible to feature, having not been included in Porto's Champions League league-phase squad.

Midfielder In-beom Hwang will face his former club after joining Porto from Feyenoord over the summer, while on-loan striker Santiago Gimenez returns to the Netherlands after representing the Dutch side between 2022 and 2025.

Ernst; Read, Kraaijeveld, Marmol, Lopez; Zechiel, Vanhoutte, Targhalline; Valente, Hadj Moussa; Ferri

#1695. FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

Home » Home 2 » FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

The ban will start from the July transfer window this year and finish with the January transfer market in 2017.

Atletico were also fined 900,000 Swiss francs (820,000 euros) and Real 360,000 (330,000 euros).

“The two clubs were found to have violated several provisions concerning the international transfer and first registration of minor players as well as other relevant provisions with regard to the registration and participation of certain players in competitions,” said a FIFA statement.

Barcelona has just ended a one year ban for similar reasons.

Real and Atletico were “issued with a reprimand and given 90 days in which to regularise the situation of all minor players concerned,” FIFA said. They can still sell players during the transfer ban.

FIFA said the alarm was raised over the two clubs by FIFA’s Transfer Matching System and its disciplinary committee completed the inquiry.

Under international football rules, players under 18 cannot be transferred to another country, except in limited circumstances. All transfers need the approval of a special FIFA committee.

“The investigations concerned minor players who were involved and participated in competitions with the clubs over various periods between 2007 and 2014 (Atletico Madrid) and between 2005 and 2014 (Real Madrid),” FIFA said.

The ban follows a similar sanction handed to European champions Barcelona, who were unable to register new players during 2015.

Barca were initially banned in April 2014, but managed to delay the sanction taking affect until the transfer windows in January and the summer 2015 by launching an ultimately unsuccessful appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

By delaying the ban, Barca managed to sign the likes of Luis Suarez and Ivan Rakitic in the summer of 2014 to propel them to a treble of La Liga, Champions League and Copa del Rey.

The news is just the latest institutional embarassment for Real Madrid just over a week after they appointed French legend Zinedine Zidane.

Madrid have sacked two Champions League winning coaches in Carlo Ancelotti and Rafael Benitez in the past seven months, as well as being thrown out of the Copa del Rey for fielding an ineligible player.

The sanction could also be bad news for the likes of Paris Saint-Germain and Manchester United, who had targeted Madrid stars Cristiano Ronaldo and Gareth Bale with Real highly unlikely to dispose of their best players without the chance to sign suitable replacements.

La Liga leaders Atletico Madrid’s usually hectic transfer policy will also be put on hold. However, Diego Simeone’s men look better placed to cope with the ban having invested heavily in young talent over the past year.

Neither Real no Atletico made an immediate comment on whether they would appeal.

#1694. Serie A preview: AC Milan vs. Frosinone – Team news, opposition insight, stats and prediction

Milan will return to action on Sunday evening, hoping to pick up where they left off before the international break with a strong performance against Frosinone.

If we look at the league, it has been a very decent start to the season for Ruben Amorim and his men. However, they are yet to win three games on the trot, so tomorrow’s encounter is a fantastic chance for them to really show their worth.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It won’t be easy, though. Amorim said during his press conference that it’s hard to identify the movement patterns of Frosinone, who certainly have the ability to make life difficult for the Rossoneri.

Game date: Sunday, November 22 Kick-off time: 18:00 (CET) Venue: San Siro Referee: Luca Pairetto (VAR: Pezzuto)

Some good news arrived on Saturday morning as Strahinja Pavlovic was deemed fit enough to be called up for the game. It’s not certain whether he will start or not, but Amorim at least said that he’s happy to have the Serbian and ‘his fire’ back.

A few days ago, it was also confirmed that Mike Maignan will be at the manager’s disposal despite the injury scare with France. Of course, it’s not all perfect on the injury front as Matteo Gabbia, Fikayo Tomori, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Alexis Saelemaekers and Samuel Chukwueze are still sidelined.

Anyway, moving on to the predicted starting eleven, it was initially thought that Amorim would field the same one as we saw against Genoa. However, he made it very clear during the presser that Musah won’t play as a left-back, so there will indeed be some changes.

According to the latest reports, the American will still start but in midfield instead, allowing Adrien Rabiot to have a slightly more advanced role. It also means that Davide Bartesaghi will come into the eleven, currently ahead of Pervis Estupinan in the race.

Alphadjo Cisse has been in red-hot form lately but it seems Amorim wants to manage expectations a little, with the youngster tipped to start on the bench. Christian Pulisic should thus have a role on the flank as opposed to in the centre, although one would imagine everything will be a bit fluid.

It’s no surprise to see that Goncalo Ramos should start up front, but of course, he will need to get going with the goalscoring sooner rather than later. Francesco Camarda is knocking on the door, as is Cisse who has been tested in that role before.

Predicted Milan XI (4-3-3): Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Diawara, Bartesaghi; Musah, Modric, Rabiot; Moreira, Ramos, Pulisic.

Predicted bench: Torriani, P. Terracciano, F. Terracciano, Pavlovic, Vladimirov, Estupinan, Jashari, Comotto, Hutchinson, Cisse, Camarda.

Injuries & suspensions: Gabbia, Tomori, Loftus-Cheek, Saelemaekers and Chukwueze.

Frosinone have definitely been one of the surprises of the season so far. After a very strong Serie B campaign with 81 points and only three games lost, they secured direct promotion to the top tier (finishing second) and have been making the most of the adventure.

They are currently on 20 points after eleven games, winning six, drawing two and losing three, which has put them in sixth place. That’s very strong for a newcomer and for a coach who is only in his second season with the club, especially considering the upset against Como.

It’s the 56-year-old’s second attempt at Serie A after coaching Cremonese for half a season in 2022-23. He didn’t manage a single win then, so you can definitely say that the performance so far has been great revenge for him.

So, what is behind this rise? As pointed out by Gazzetta dello Sport, the direct style of play has been key for Frosinone. As opposed to Milan, who want to see a lot of the ball, they are willing to have less possession and break on the counter.

It doesn’t mean that they sit back, though. In fact, it has been the opposite as they are the highest-pressing team in the league. The strategy thus seems to be to force mistakes out of the opponents, while also making sure that they are direct in possession.

While collective effort deserves most of the praise, it has definitely helped that the likes of Giacomo Calo, Giorgi Kvernadze and Antonio Raimondo – among others – have performed at a very high level. They aren’t exactly big-name players, so a lot of them are having their breakout seasons.

Moving on to actual team news, the situation up front is not ideal for Frosinone as their top scorer, the aforementioned Antonio Raimondo, is out injured. Birigilea, who is on two goals, is set to replace him in the No.9 position.

The Milan academy product Sebastiano Desplanches, who left the club four years ago, will be on the bench. He’s yet to make an appearance this season, with Alvini preferring Lorenzo Palmisani instead.

Predicted Frosinone XI (4-2-3-1): Palmisani; Oyono, Calvani, Monterisi, Terzic; Calo, Masini; Ghedjemis; Schmid, Kvernadze; Birigilea.

Predicted bench: Desplanches, Pisseri, Cittadini, Tchato, Amey, Akpoguma, Fayed, El Azzouzi, Cichella, Hasa, Fini, Zerbin, Bobcek.

Injuries & suspensions: Bracaglia, Grillitsch and Raimondo.

This fixture has only been played six times, but even with such a small sample size, it’s clear that Milan are the favourites with four wins and two draws so far. They have won the last three as well, spread across the 2023-24 and 2018-19 seasons.

That said, the most recent encounter was a dramatic one, if you like. Olivier Giroud opened the scoring for Milan away from home but then Frosinone scored twice. Thanks to goals from Matteo Gabbia and Luka Jovic, the Rossoneri were able to turn it back in their favour.

The last time at San Siro, meanwhile, it was a great 3-1 win as Jovic, Pulisic and Tomori found the back of the net. Most of you will remember the American’s goal, as it was Maignan who assisted him with a fantastic pass.

➤ Milan are unbeaten in all six previous meetings against Frosinone in Serie A (W4 D2): among the teams against which they have never lost in the competition, the Rossoneri have played more games only against Pisa (14 – six also against Crotone and Lecco).

➤ Milan have scored at least three goals in four of their six Serie A matches against Frosinone, producing 15 goals overall, an average of 2.5 per game. Only against Pescara (2.9) have they recorded a higher average, among the opponents they have faced on at least five occasions (2.5 also against Casale and Messina).

➤ Frosinone have won six games this season, drawing two and losing three. Only three newly promoted teams in the last 40 years have recorded more wins in their first 12 Serie A games of the season: Bari in 1994/95 (seven), Chievo in 2001/02 (seven), and Hellas Verona in 2013/14 (seven).

➤ Milan have won four of their last five league games (L1), scoring at least two goals in each, after failing to win three of their previous four (D3). The last time they scored more than one goal in consecutive Serie A matches was between September 2020 and January 2021, when they managed 15 games.

➤ Although Frosinone are unbeaten in three of their five away games this season (W1 D2), they have won just two of their last 27 away games in Serie A (including previous participations), with 10 draws and 15 defeats.

➤ Milan have failed to win four of their last seven Serie A games played after the international break (D2 L2). On the other hand, Frosinone are unbeaten in three of their last five top-flight matches immediately following Italy matches (W2 D1).

➤ Frosinone have attempted the most counterattacks from advantageous situations in Serie A this season: 22, almost double the number of any other team. On the other hand, Milan are the only team that haven’t allowed a single counterattack when trailing in the current campaign.

➤ Only Juventus (79) have attempted more long-range shots than Frosinone (77) this season. On the other hand, Milan are the team that have attempted the fewest shots from outside the area (30) and the one that have conceded the most shots from outside the area in relation to the total conceded, 44%.

➤ Adrien Rabiot has earned the most points for his team from direct goal contributions this season, having scored 10 goals and assisted four times. In the most recent matchday, he became the first Milan midfielder to be involved in at least one goal in six consecutive league appearances since Kaká in 2004 (who managed seven).

➤ Only Matías Soulé (80) has been involved in more sequences ending with a shot than Giacomo Calò (76) in this Serie A. The Frosinone player has scored five goals in the current campaign and only one midfielder has scored more goals in the first 12 matchdays in the top flight for a newly promoted team in the three points for a win era: Hidetoshi Nakata with Perugia in 1998/99 (six).

Since Frosinone like to play on the counterattacks, one player who I think could be crucial for Milan is Musah. As he’s set to start in midfield and not at left-back, the feeling is that his main role will be to prevent the opponents from having too much open space on the counter.

Further up the pitch, I’m excited to see Moreira. He got himself a goal in Belgium’s win over Italy and he has looked a lot better on the right flank ever since the derby performance. He can definitely make the difference with his skill.

As for Frosinone, it’s obvious that Calo is the man whom Milan will want to stop. He likes to dictate the play and if he’s allowed too much time on the ball, identifying his teammates in good positions, then there could be trouble for the Rossoneri.

It will also be interesting to see if Birigilea can fill the shoes of Raimondo. He bagged a brace against Lecce but in the last two games, he failed to find the back of the net. He will surely be keen to get back on target.

A lot of people are expecting this to be a high-scoring affair and that’s a very reasonable take, given how both teams play. That said, I think this could be one where Milan actually get their defence in order and don’t concede, even if that might be a somewhat optimistic prediction.

If Andoni Iraola had been allowed to write the script for this game, it would probably have played out in broadly similar fashion.

Liverpool came into their latest clash with bitter rivals Manchester United having enjoyed a healthy start under the Basque, yet with a few question marks still over them.

That is exactly why this victory was extra sweet for Iraola, because his team answered each of them across the course of an enjoyable afternoon at Anfield.

The first concerned a poor home record that had seen the Reds take just five points from a possible 15, and which was clearly enhanced here.

The second related to their record in big games thanks to recent defeats to Manchester City and Arsenal.

Yes, United are in a tricky spot at the moment, but it can never be said that a meeting between England's two biggest clubs is not 'big'.

The third, meanwhile, was about whether Liverpool had shown enough in terms of free-flowing football, and they surely answered that in tearing the Red Devils apart here, largely through the electric Rio Ngumoha.

As such, it is surely only fair to take this result and performance at face value, as Iraola and his players likely will.

That means they will come away from this afternoon feeling like they are a team building momentum under a new manager, which is exactly what they are.

#1688. Rio Ngumoha breaks Premier League record in Liverpool win vs Man Utd

By Saikat Mandal | 22 Nov 2026 18:54, Last updated: 22 Nov 2026 19:40

Liverpool produced arguably their finest performance under Andoni Iraola as they thrashed Manchester United 4-0 in Sunday's Premier League clash at Anfield.

The victory keeps the Reds third in the Premier League table, but they have closed the gap on Manchester City to one point and remain seven points adrift of leaders Arsenal.

Just eight minutes into Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge, the Red Devils were reduced to 10 men after Leny Yoro was shown a straight red card for a challenge on Alexander Isak.

From the resulting free kick, Dominik Szoboszlai fired Liverpool into the lead, before the hosts strengthened their advantage when Florian Wirtz finished off a brilliant move down the flank involving Rio Ngumoha.

The Reds youngster got on the scoresheet himself in the second half, while substitute Victor Munoz put the finishing touches on a commanding display by netting the fourth goal.

With Cody Gakpo unavailable, Iraola handed Ngumoha a place in the starting lineup, and the youngster delivered an electrifying performance on the night.

According to Opta Joe, Ngumoha became the youngest player ever to register a goal involvement in a Premier League match between Liverpool and Manchester United.

Picking up possession, he bamboozled his marker before whipping in a superb left-footed cross, which Wirtz emphatically converted to put Liverpool 2-0 ahead.

After the break, Bradley Barcola escaped his marker and played a perfectly weighted pass into Ngumoha's path, leaving the youngster with a simple finish.

In doing so, Ngumoha also became the youngest player to score and provide an assist in a Premier League match since Michael Owen achieved the feat on Boxing Day 1997.

Reports have emerged in recent weeks suggesting that Bayern Munich remain interested in signing Ngumoha, but Liverpool should not entertain any offers for the highly-rated youngster.

Ngumoha is already receiving more opportunities under Iraola and is expected to play a significant role this season.

Liverpool rate him highly, and there is little doubt that he could develop into a regular first-team fixture as he continues to mature.

While Yoro's dismissal certainly helped Liverpool take control of the contest, Man Utd offered little to trouble the hosts and failed to frustrate them by remaining resolute at the back.
