#1563. Player Ratings: AC Milan 5-1 Frosinone – Rabiot unstoppable; super attack

AC Milan clinched a comfortable win against Frosinone and individual brilliance certainly had a hand in that. Below are the player ratings for the Rossoneri.

Ahead of what will be a busy month, Milan knew that a win tonight would do them a lot of good, so that’s exactly what they managed to achieve. Goals from Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic set them up nicely, as well as an early own-goal.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

If you haven’t already, make sure to check out how we decide the player ratings. From the scale to what affects the rating, we have compiled everything there.

🥇 Rabiot (8 – MOTM): He just can’t help himself from getting goal contributions! Two more assists today, three if you count the own-goal, and his running is becoming a proper weapon for Milan. He’s just unstoppable when he gets going.

👔 Amorim (7.5): I think this was more or less a home run tactically. Frosinone were always going to try to have a high line, so the head coach exploited that with the help of Rabiot and the passing abilities of his teammates. Benching Cisse was bold, but it turned out to be just the right move.

Maignan (6): I’m not sure he could have done better on the goal, as it was really hard to predict where the cross would end up. Anyway, he made a couple of decent stops and was good with his feet, even if there was a scare in the first half.

Gila (6.5): Let me just say straight off the bat that he wasn’t far away from a 7. However, I think he could have done better to stop the cross on the goal conceded, and he had a few really poor passes as well. On the plus side, he was decent in possession overall and had a key clearance in the second half.

De Winter (6.5): He continues to marshal the defence well, though he lacked concentration on a few occasions today. It didn’t prove to be costly and similarly to Gila, there was definitely more good than harm, but the rating is affected a tad.

Diawara (6.5): I don’t think he could have got to the ball quicker on the goal, not to mention that it’s hard to anticipate such a deflection. As far as I’m concerned, it was solid defending from him, including some nice clearances to stop a few dangerous crosses.

Bartesaghi (6): Defensively he did okay, which was all that was required of him, but the main contributions were in attack. I think we saw some really good runs forward from him, although the crosses had mixed results. It seems fair with a 6 for him.

Moreira (7.5): His run before the second goal was crucial, of course, and he also managed to get an assist (good pass in the end, as VAR confirmed). For a higher rating, I would have liked to see more sharpness in the final third, as he had a couple of very good shooting opportunities that he missed.

Modric (8): My word, the pass before the first goal was just magnificent! That alone shows just how much he means to this team, but he also continued to do well with his passing and movement after that. For me, the rating does deserve to be that high, but maybe I’m blinded by the aforementioned pass.

Musah (7): He did really well to unleash Moreira just before the second goal, playing it perfectly. On the goal conceded, it was just unlucky in my opinion, he did everything right by getting a toe on it. The block at the start of the second half was just brilliant too, showcasing good defensive skills.

Pulisic (7.5): Amorim always says he lets the pitch do the talking and that was the case today. He wasn’t flashy by any means, but did very good work in silence (such as the movement before the own-goal) and was eventually rewarded with the goal. Stunning finish by the way. An 8 perhaps?

Rabiot (8 – MOTM): He just can’t help himself from getting goal contributions! Two more assists today, three if you count the own-goal, and his running is becoming a proper weapon for Milan. He’s just unstoppable when he gets going.

Ramos (7.5): Finally, back on target! Overall, it was a very encouraging one for him as the goal was the result of great positioning and hard work, which helped on the other goals too (opening up space). He could have had a second too if he hadn’t been stopped by the referee.

Jashari (7): That’s one way to make an impact! The finish was fantastic and really surprised the goalkeeper. He had a few more good runs after that, so this was definitely a performance that he can build on.

Cisse (7): It was an easy finish on the goal, it has to be said, but he still timed the run very well. He also showed off some good understanding in the centre-forward, which was nice to see. It wasn’t nice to see the unnecessary yellow card at the end, though.

#1562. Man City injury news: Latest Matheus Nunes update from Enzo Maresca before Napoli clash

By Oliver Thomas | 23 Nov 2026 12:42

Enzo Maresca has provided a positive injury update on Manchester City’s Matheus Nunes ahead of Tuesday’s Champions League clash with Napoli at the Etihad Stadium.

The 28-year-old was unable to recover in time from an ankle problem to feature in City’s 1-1 Premier League draw with Fulham on Saturday.

Nunes has been absent for four of the Citizens’ last seven games in all tournaments this term, but Maresca confirmed at a pre-match press conference on Monday that the right-back “is back” and ready to face Napoli.

"Matheus is back. Then the only one [out] is still Antoine [Semenyo],” Maresca told reporters. “The rest, we have some doubts in terms of tiredness, amount of games, and we have today's session and then we'll decide."

Pushed for more details on Nunes’s recent injury, Maresca added: "This one has been a little bit his ankle, but now he's fine. It's also normal with the amount of games we have, that's why also sometimes I try to rotate players.

"I've said many times, we need to not think about a sprint, we need to think about a marathon; 65 games. So I would like to use the strongest one every game, but then we destroy them. It's also a matter of trying to manage them the best way.”

Nunes has established himself as Man City’s first-choice right-back when fit and available, while Abdukodir Khusanov and Rico Lewis have also been used on the right side of defence under Maresca and predecessor Pep Guardiola.

Man City’s No.27 has played 10 times across all competitions so far this season, but he has been left out of the matchday squad for five games due to injury or fitness-related issues.

"Since we started, we've used Rico [Lewis at right-back], but also [Khusanov], who I think he can play there,” Maresca explained. “For sure, it's much better... I'm trying to find the right balance.

"If you ask me if Khusa is a better right-back or central defender, no doubt: Central defender. I know that. But it's a matter of the game, the players we have available.

"But Matheus [Nunes] has done very good since we started, the games he has played, overall he was very good. Rico has [also] done very good so far.”

It remains to be seen whether Maresca will throw Nunes straight back into the starting lineup against Napoli, with one eye possibly on Sunday’s important Premier League showdown with Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium.

Man City have won three of their first four Champions League games in the League Phase and can strengthen their automatic last-16 qualification hopes with a victory against Napoli, who have lost three of their opening four matches in the competition.

#1561. Villa Midfielder Has £80m Price Tag For Arsenal: Is He Worth It?

Arsenal transfer news: Aston Villa do not regard Boubacar Kamara as available, even with Arsenal interested, according to CaughtOffside. The report says an offer of around £80m could change that stance, although Villa negotiate from strength because the 26-year-old’s contract runs until 2030.

January looks highly unlikely. Villa have already lost Amadou Onana to a torn ACL suffered at the World Cup, and the Belgian is not expected back until around April. Unai Emery cannot lose a second holding midfielder in the middle of a season. The summer is different. CaughtOffside says Villa could entertain a significant bid then, provided they can reinvest the money in a proper replacement and strengthen the squad around him.

TBR Football reported in July 2025 that he sat on Arsenal’s long list of midfield targets, and his numbers explain why. Kamara has started all 10 of his Premier League games this season, completing 86.3% of his passes, including 83 line-breaking balls, while making 28 tackles and 40 recoveries. He wins 56% of his duels and can play at centre-back, which would give Mikel Arteta cover in two positions.

The weaknesses are just as clear. He has no goals this season, only three shots and an xG of 0.14, and he has committed 20 fouls and conceded a penalty. He also missed the closing weeks of 2024/25 through injury.

The role he would play is obvious: a ball-playing six next to Declan Rice. Martín Zubimendi occupies it now, and Arsenal lead the league with 27 points from 10 games, six clear of Manchester City, with seven clean sheets.

No, not at that price. Arsenal spent £75m on Bruno Guimarães in August, and Arteta still has Rice, Zubimendi, Mikel Merino, Martin Ødegaard and Myles Lewis-Skelly competing for the same central spaces.

FotMob values him at €49m, roughly £43m, so Villa would be asking close to double his market value for a player who turns 27 this month and offers little in the final third. Villa’s insistence on reinvesting the fee also hands them the leverage, which means Arsenal would pay a premium on a seller’s timetable.

The only sensible trigger is a departure, perhaps Zubimendi or the 30-year-old Merino, leaving Arsenal short of a proven Premier League six. Kamara is a better holding midfielder than most of the market, but a title-leading side already has that job covered, and £80m would buy cover rather than improvement.

#1560. Man City sign Enzo Fernandez for £125m to end transfer saga of the summer

Manchester City have equalled the British record transfer on deadline day after agreeing to pay £125m to sign midfielder Enzo Fernández from Chelsea.

The deal brings to an end the biggest saga of the summer and means that Enzo Maresca, the new City head coach, has landed his number one target.

City left it until the last day of the transfer window to strike an agreement after Chelsea decided that Fernández’s exit was in the best interests of the club. But a late move to replace the Argentine with Monaco midfielder Lamie Camara collapsed to the anger of the Premier League club, leaving Xabi Alonso one player light among his midfield options.

Having refused to meet Chelsea’s self-imposed deadline to sign Fernández for £120m earlier in the summer, City had to equal the £125m Liverpool paid Newcastle United for Alexander Isak 12 months earlier.

Fernández had made it clear that he wanted to leave Chelsea some time ago and was left out of Alonso’s squad for the victories last week over Luton Town, in the Carabao Cup, and Brighton.

Having initially wanted to join Real Madrid, Fernández set his heart on linking back up with Maresca at City. The pair share a close relationship and had kept in touch after Maresca left Chelsea at the start of the year.

This is the second time Fernández has become the most expensive player in British transfer history, having previously set the record when he joined Chelsea for £107m from Benfica in the 2023 winter window.

Introducing our new Argentinian Blue 🇦🇷🩵 pic.twitter.com/nEHQ1oM855

During his time at Chelsea, 25-year-old Fernández won the Club World Cup and the Europa Conference League but he was also at the centre of controversy.

In January 2025, Fernández posted a video of himself and some of his Argentina international team-mates singing an offensive song about France players of African origin after winning the Copa America. He apologised to his Chelsea team-mates and made a donation to an anti-discrimination charity, but was still made the team’s vice-captain.

Last season was Fernández’s best goalscoring campaign, as he netted 15 goals in all competitions for Chelsea but the club finished 10th in the Premier League table. In April, he was suspended for two games by the club for suggesting he would like to live in Madrid – which was perceived as a come and get me plea to Real Madrid.

He angered England fans with his celebration after scoring against Thomas Tuchel’s team in Argentina’s World Cup semi-final victory over England, before being sent-off in the final defeat by Spain.

Chelsea fans booed Fernández in pre-season, although the club’s travelling supporters sang his name when he was introduced as a substitute in the victory over Fulham at the start of this season.

Fernández thanked his team-mates and the Chelsea staff in an emotional farewell post on Instagram. He added: “I want you to know that these have not been easy days for me. Writing this is not easy either. The truth is, I haven’t been in a good place.

“Three years ago, Cobham and Stamford Bridge became home for me and my family. I grew attached to the people, to the shirt, and to the badge of this incredible club.

“Believe me when I say that, from the moment I arrived, I became obsessed with winning and with bringing this club every trophy that its history deserves. We suffered, we cried, I got angry many times, but we also celebrated titles and unforgettable victories. Together, through the good times and the difficult ones.

“I live football the same way I live my life: with passion and with all my heart. That is why I want you to know that I understand you. I truly understand you, from the bottom of my heart.

“But life is about making decisions, and right now I find myself having to make one of those difficult decisions. I’ve said it before, but I want to say it again: I have grown incredibly fond of this club. Chelsea will always have a place in my thoughts and, above all, in my heart.

“But I also understand how football works. I know how passionate you are, because I am the same. And if I were in your position, I would probably be thinking the same way.”

Proper City 🤩🩵 pic.twitter.com/TfRTZOnPrw

The sale of Fernández means that Chelsea have set a new British transfer record of their own, having secured more than £500m in sales and loan fees during the summer transfer window.

Chelsea set about spending some of the money made from the Fernández sale by agreeing a last-minute deal for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara.

Monaco had rejected a bid of £38.5m from Chelsea on deadline day, but an improved offer of £47m was accepted late on Tuesday night, only to be called off by Monaco on the stroke of the 11pm deadline.

Chelsea had been able to complete a medical during negotiations and Camara agreed to a six-year contract with the option of a further year to bolster Alonso’s midfield options, but he will now not join the club.

Chelsea had also seen at least one offer for Bournemouth’s Alex Scott rejected this summer, while the club showed an interest in Roma’s Manu Kone and explored whether or not a move for Arsenal’s Martin Zubimendi would be possible earlier this month.

Chilly tonight... pic.twitter.com/VihgKCScfn

The 21-year-old midfielder who came through the ranks at Real Madrid has been signed from Stuttgart.

Brighton’s sporting director Mike Cave said: “We’re delighted to welcome Chema to the club. He has an excellent pedigree having come through at Real Madrid; he followed that with a very good season with Stuttgart last season.

“We had been aware of Chema’s potential for sometime, and we are delighted to welcome him to the club, and look forward to working with him.”

Fernandez says: “Manchester City are the most successful club in England in recent times.

“Every player wants to be part of a club like this because everyone knows how well-run City are.

“I could not be happier to be here, and I am ready for the challenge of helping City continue winning trophies. This is a club built for success.

“If you look across the squad, City have quality in every area. I want to learn from my new teammates and become a better player.

Introducing our new Argentinian Blue 🇦🇷🩵 pic.twitter.com/nEHQ1oM855

In this scrupulously detailed account of Arsenal’s summer, Sam Dean assesses where things went right, and wrong, for the Premier League champions in the transfer market.

They have buttressed the two areas in which they were already strong by signing Bruno Guimaraes and Ezri Konsa, but failed to sign the level-raising forward Mikel Arteta coveted.

In fact, with Gabriel Jesus, Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli departing (as well as Ethan Nwaneri moving on loan), their weakest department is arguably weaker than this time last year. Christos Tzolis, signed for £34m from Club Brugge, is their only attacking purchase.

But I also understand how football works. I know how passionate you are, because I am the same. And if I were in your position, I would probably be thinking the same way.

I want to thank every single one of you: the staff, the coaching team, the medical team, the physios, and everyone who works at Cobham and throughout this great institution.

To all my teammates over these years, thank you from the bottom of my heart for sharing so many moments with me. I was truly happy here, and I wish you nothing but the very best for the future.

Thank you for all the love and support you have given me and my family throughout these years. I will never forget it.

This group will give you many more reasons to be happy, and I will be happy for you too. Never doubt that.

You will always be in my heart, Blues. I will always wish you, always, nothing but the very best.

I want you to know that these have not been easy days for me. Writing this is not easy either. The truth is, I haven’t been in a good place.

Three years ago, Cobham and Stamford Bridge became home for me and my family. I grew attached to the people, to the shirt, and to the badge of this incredible club.

Believe me when I say that, from the moment I arrived, I became obsessed with winning and with bringing this club every trophy that its history deserves. We suffered, we cried, I got angry many times, but we also celebrated titles and unforgettable victories. Together, through the good times and the difficult ones.

I live football the same way I live my life: with passion and with all my heart. That is why I want you to know that I understand you. I truly understand you, from the bottom of my heart.

But life is about making decisions, and right now I find myself having to make one of those difficult decisions. I’ve said it before, but I want to say it again: I have grown incredibly fond of this club. Chelsea will always have a place in my thoughts and, above all, in my heart.

Crystal Palace have agreed a deal to re-sign Ben Chilwell. The 29-year-old was on loan at Palace last year and deal struck with Strasbourg for him to leave French club and return to the Premier League.

Sunderland were involved in the most bewildering transfer of the summer on deadline day as they fought a day-long tug-of-war with Crystal Palace for winger Malick Fofana.

On a day of claims and counterclaims, Sunderland have finally triumphed in the battle to land the Belgium international just an hour before the deadline.

But despite their success, it was a transfer that will leave a sour taste in the mouth to many, with the player repeatedly changing his mind about which club he wanted to join

As the saga dragged on, it is understood Fofana had a medical in Lyon with both Sunderland and Crystal Palace given access to the information as he still could not decide which club to join as talks continued into the evening.

Sunderland had a bid of around £25m accepted by Lyon on Tuesday morning and thought they had an agreement with both the player and his agent on personal terms and fees only for Palace to make a late attempt to hijack the deal.

The London club’s manager, Pierre Sage, who worked with Fofana at Lyon, is thought to have personally intervened in an attempt to persuade the player to move to South London. By late afternoon, Palace appeared to have got their man having also offered more money to Lyon and higher wages to the player and fees to his agency.

Sunderland, though, refused to concede defeat and, according to reports in France, launched a counter proposal of their own led by French owners Kyril Louis-Dreyfus who flew to Lyon to try and clinch the deal.

At one stage, it was even claimed that the player had two different private jets waiting at the airport to take him to either London or the North East depending on who he elected to sign for.

That was later refuted, although it is understood the player did have a medical in Lyon that could be viewed by both clubs before he made up his mind. That gave his representatives more time to thrash the terms of a deal with both clubs.

However, having failed to board an earlier flight to Lyon after talks with Palace advanced, Sunderland’s late push belatedly persuaded the 21-year-old to head to Wearside, and he is due to be unveiled on Wednesday morning.

Arsenal had also been linked with the player earlier this week but were not willing to match the asking price for Fofana who they viewed as a project player.

Forgive the personal opinion but this is my favourite deal of the window. Mudryk played some of his best football under Roberto De Zerbi at Shakhtar Donetsk. The Spurs head coach has even described Mudryk as “my son”, and has previously tipped him as a future Ballon d’Or winner.

After so long out of the game, Mudryk now has a coach who knows exactly how to get the best out of him. It might not work at all. Mudryk may need months to rediscover his match sharpness after so long out. But I am very excited to find out.

Will there be any incomings? The Julian Alvarez situation seems unlikely to develop in Arsenal’s favour, barring a dramatic change of heart. As reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday, Lyon winger Malick Fofana is a potential option.

It is expected to be another busy deadline day in the Premier League, with many clubs still hoping to finalise deals before the transfer window shuts at 11pm. Here, Telegraph Sport identifies 10 potential high-profile moves that could yet go through.

This has been the most dramatic and relentless saga of the European transfer window. The situation, as far as we understand it, is as follows: Barcelona want Alvarez and Alvarez wants Barcelona, but Atletico Madrid refuse to sell him to Barcelona. Arsenal want Alvarez, and Atletico are more open to selling him to Arsenal, but Alvarez only wants Barcelona. For a move to happen, it will require one party to change their mind. Either Atletico decides to sell to Barcelona, or Alvarez decides he will join Arsenal.

Another long-running saga. Chelsea are well aware of City’s interest in Fernandez but want a massive fee for the Argentina international, having initially valued him at £120m. City have the cash and the space in the squad after saying goodbye to Rodri, Tijani Reijnders, Nico Gonzalez and Bernardo Silva this summer. Fernandez has not featured in Chelsea’s last two games.

As reported by Telegraph Sport last week, Chelsea have identified Monaco midfielder Camara as a target amid the uncertainty over Fernandez’s future. French reports on Monday suggested the move may have stalled, however. The clock is ticking.

Spurs had been working on a deal to sign Ndiaye from Everton but they now appear to have fallen behind City in the race for the winger, as a consequence of City failing in their attempt to sign Cody Gakpo from Liverpool. City are ready to complete the hijack on deadline day.

A deal that, as of Monday night, is regarded as unlikely to happen. As with their interest in Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh, Liverpool have so far been unable to strike a deal with Crystal Palace for Sarr, who scored 21 goals in 45 games last season. Liverpool would only allow Gakpo to leave if a replacement, such as Sarr, can be signed.

Burnley are one of a host of Championship clubs who are interested in the young Manchester United left-back Harry Amass. There have been talks over a potential permanent deal but a loan cannot be ruled out. The 19-year-old joined United from Watford in 2023.

Everton have reached an agreement with Manchester City to sign Jack Grealish on another season long loan. It has been a very busy summer of outgoings at City and Grealish will be the latest to depart as he prepares to return to Merseyside. He started well at Everton last season before injury in January derailed his campaign.

A big year ahead for the English midfielder.

Tottenham are set to complete a double deal for Chelsea pair Mykhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo after missing out on Iliman Ndiaye.

Spurs will take Mudryk on loan for the season having seen their attempt to land Ndiaye fail when Manchester City agreed a £65m deal with Everton.

Mudryk, 25, worked with Spurs head coach Roberto De Zerbi at Shakthtar Donetsk, in the winger’s homeland Ukraine, before his £85m move to Chelsea in 2023.

Leeds United had shown interest but instead he will be reunited with De Zerbi, effectively taking Ndiaye’s place as a wide-forward option.

Adarabioyo will be a permanent deal to Spurs as they are not allowed to loan two players from a Premier League club.

Good morning and welcome to live coverage of transfer deadline day. We are deep into stoppage time in this summer window and we will bring you the key developments as teams scramble to get last-minute deals over the line before the full-time whistle blows at 11pm.

Enzo Fernández remains a City target, and his omission from Xabi Alonso’s match-day squad against Brighton and Hove Albion on Sunday has only added weight to the feeling that he might reunite with former Chelsea head coach Enzo Maresca. City would be required to meet the Londoners’ £120m asking price, which is just shy of Alexander Isak’s £125m British record fee.

Meanwhile, Julián Alvarez’s situation at Atlético Madrid continues to be monitored by Arsenal. The Argentina forward’s dream move to Barcelona appears a no-goer as Atlético remain steadfast in their refusal to sell to their La Liga rivals. While this could bring Arsenal into the picture, it is understood that Alvarez – who missed three training sessions last week and did not travel to Sevilla with Diego Simeone’s squad on Saturday – is not pursuing a return to England.

A Mohamed Salah-shaped hole on Liverpool’s right flank has been filled by Bradley Barcola after the club agreed a £123m deal with Paris St-Germain. His signing looked as though it might trigger Cody Gakpo’s move away from Anfield as the winger had been linked with a move to Manchester City, but it appears that the Netherlands international will stay put. Maresca’s side have instead hijacked Spurs’ move for Iliman Ndiaye, and the north London outfit pivoted to take Myhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo from Chelsea, on loan and permanent deals respectively. Liverpool could yet swoop for Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh or Ismaïla Sarr.

Newcastle United appeared to have reached their nadir this summer after Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimarães and Eddie Howe departed, but Matthias Jaissle has breathed life into St James’ Park by delivering an exciting brand of football that leans on the team’s explosive pace in forward positions. Lille’s Matias Fernandez-Pardo would fit this system and is on the brink of joining Newcastle in a deal worth £51m, which could signal Nick Woltemade’s exit.

Barcola is the window’s most expensive acquisition, followed by Morgan Rogers who was prised away from Aston Villa to the tune of £118m, and has already hit the ground running for the Londoners. He cost £2m more than his England team-mate Elliot Anderson, who swapped Nottingham Forest for Manchester City. Elite midfielders have proved a gilded commodity with seven of the Premier League’s top 10 most expensive acquisitions coming in the middle of the park. The departures of Rodri, Casemiro and others will have played their part.

Praying for a deadline-day saviour or counting down the seconds until the window slams shut on directors of football hoping to lure away your club’s next big thing? Let us know in the comments and join the conversation as the day unfolds.

#1559. Man Utd transfer news: First player to depart Old Trafford in January 'revealed'

By Saikat Mandal | 23 Nov 2026 12:44

Manchester United striker Joshua Zirkzee could reportedly become the first player to leave Old Trafford during the January transfer window.

The Dutchman joined the Red Devils from Bologna in the summer of 2024 and has since made 86 appearances for the club across all competitions.

Zirkzee has managed just 11 goals and four assists for Man Utd and was heavily linked with a move away from the club during the summer transfer window.

Several Serie A clubs were keen to sign him, with Fiorentina reportedly agreeing a loan fee for the striker, but the proposed move ultimately failed to materialise.

Premier League rivals Everton also made a late push for the 25-year-old, but Man Utd were unwilling to let him leave without first securing a replacement.

Former Man Utd manager Michael Carrick even suggested that Zirkzee could become an important player for the club, but the striker has since slipped considerably down the pecking order.

According to La Gazzetta dello Sport (via Manchester Evening News), Zirkzee is expected to become the first player to depart in January, with several Italian clubs competing for his signature.

Juventus and Fiorentina are reportedly keen to sign the striker, while Napoli could also enter the race.

The former Bayern Munich attacker has made just seven substitute appearances in the Premier League this season, accumulating 134 minutes of action and scoring once.

Zirkzee has also featured three times as a substitute in the Champions League, where he has registered another goal.

Mauricio Pochettino introduced him in the second half of Man Utd's 4-0 defeat against Liverpool, and the Dutchman managed to make a positive impression despite the disappointing result.

Towards the end of the contest, Zirkzee produced a brilliant pass to Bruno Fernandes, but the United captain's effort was comfortably saved by Alisson Becker.

If Zirkzee fails to earn more opportunities under Pochettino over the coming month, the likelihood of him leaving Old Trafford could increase considerably.

#1558. Chelsea’s £43m Winger Gamble Is Stalling: Should They Accept A Discount?

Chelsea transfer news: Birmingham Live reports that Alejandro Garnacho’s future needs resolving, because the winger has not started a match for Aston Villa and a permanent move depends on certain conditions being met. Chelsea sent the 22-year-old to Villa Park on a season-long loan in July, with a reported £43m obligation to buy next summer. Neither club has revealed the trigger, and reports link it to appearances.

The numbers explain the concern. FotMob lists four Premier League outings, all from the bench, without a goal or assist, while Football365 counts only 95 minutes across seven substitute appearances. Football Insider claims Villa are prepared to back out of the deal if his form doesn’t improve.

Garnacho’s strengths haven’t changed. His pace, directness and willingness to take on defenders earned a £40m move from Manchester United in 2025. The weakness is end product, and it followed him to London with eight goals in 43 games for Chelsea, only one of them in 24 Premier League appearances. Unai Emery left him out of the squad for the Manchester United game.

Chelsea have no obvious use for him either. Xabi Alonso told him in July that regular football wasn’t guaranteed, and the 3-4-2-1 Alonso favours uses Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer behind João Pedro, with Pedro Neto and Estêvão competing for the wide roles.

FotMob values him at about €29m (roughly £25m), far below the €71m peak recorded in August 2024, and Manchester United are reportedly entitled to 10 per cent of any future fee. If the clause isn’t triggered, he returns in July 2027 on a contract running to 2032.

Yes, and soon. Chelsea built the deal to protect £43m, but the clause relies on appearances from a manager who isn’t picking him, so the price drops with every unused substitution. The sporting case for a return is thin. Alonso’s system asks wide players to defend as wing-backs, while Garnacho’s value lies in isolating a full-back, and the £117m Rogers signing already covers the left-sided attacking role.

A mid-£20m sale, even after United’s cut, would still return more than half of the £40m Chelsea paid and clear a contract running to 2032. Chelsea should open talks with Villa in January about a lower fixed fee, or line up other buyers for the summer. A clause that depends on a manager picking a player he has benched was never a safe way to protect £43m.

#1557. Cardinale praises ‘fantastic’ Milan and admits he ‘expects to compete’ for the Scudetto

Gerry Cardinale gave his thoughts after watching his AC Milan side run riot against Frosinone at San Siro this evening.

It has been yet another few days where the Milan owner has made his presence felt. After landing in Italy, he was at Milanello and Casa Milan on Saturday for a series of important meetings with the management and the squad, and then he watched first hand as the Rossoneri won tonight.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

An own-goal from Gabriele Calvani got the scoring going, before Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic all scored in the 5-1 rout of Frosinone. It could have been more in truth, but it was another display of the level this team can play at.

Cardinale was interviewed by Michael Cuomo of TeleLombardia after the final whistle having made his way down from the stands, and his comments were relayed by MilanNews.

“Well, I’m never satisfied, but the results speak for themselves. The boys were fantastic tonight. I hope you’re happy. I hope the fans are happy. I think the team is coming together really well.

“It’s a game, let’s keep it under control, but I’m really proud of the boys. This is a team. It’s a team that wants to win until the end.”

“Look, it’s November. We still have a long way to go. But we want to see improvements in every match. This weekend was very interesting if you look at the kind of results we’ve had. You can see that something is changing in Serie A.

“I was very happy to see us not just win, but win by that margin. And so, we have to build on that, but as Amorim says, every match is something to build on, and we have a long way to go. I personally still expect us to compete for the Scudetto, but it’s a long way off. One match at a time.

“Now the focus is on the Europa League. Yes, and as Ruben said, we have to do both. European competitions are important. Everything is a test. If you want to win a Scudetto, you have to do it all the way, and that’s what we’ll do.”

“Again: January is just another stage. As you know, the January transfer window is complicated. You have to be disciplined. You can’t just jump into something randomly. The only thing that will happen under my ownership is that every time we play in the transfer market, we’ll play to win.

“That’s the theme. That’s the theme I said at the beginning of this year. So, if we make a move in any transfer window, January or June, it will be a move that will count.”

#1556. The wild life of Peter Storey who died aged 81: An Arsenal double-winning legend who was jailed for three years for his role in a criminal counterfeit operation, once ran a brothel and was caught trying to smuggle adult films into the UK

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 11:40 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 11:55 EST, 18 November 2026

Those connected with Arsenal and England in particular, as well as Fulham, were in mourning on Tuesday following news of Peter Storey's death, aged 81.

The former right back and defensive midfielder died in hospital after a short illness, surrounded by his family.

Arsenal confirmed that the club will pay their respects at their Champions League match against Borussia Dortmund - which is their first home match post the international break - which takes place on November 24.

A club statement read: 'Everyone at Arsenal is deeply saddened by the passing of 1970-71 double winner, Peter Storey.

'All our thoughts are with his family and loved ones at this incredibly sad time. Rest in peace, Peter.'

Storey enjoyed a stellar career at Arsenal, becoming a bona-fide legend in north London and earning a reputation as a tough tackler.

Arsenal legend Peter Storey died aged 81 on Tuesday in hospital after a short illness

He played 501 games for Arsenal - placing him eighth on their all-time appearances list

Joining the club as an apprentice in 1961, he made his first-team debut against Leicester City in October 1965. That outing was the first of 501 appearances for the club - a tally which places him eighth on their all-time list.

A tough tackler, Storey moved from right back to central midfield - playing a key role in their Fairs Cup triumph in 1970.

During the 1970-71 campaign, Storey was part of the Arsenal side which completed the double and played an important part in their FA Cup success.

He scored a stoppage-time penalty against Stoke in the semi-finals to force a replay and the Gunners subsequently went on to lift the trophy.

Storey left the Gunners in 1977, scoring 19 goals across his time at the club, and moved to Fulham before retiring in 1978.

On the international stage, Storey was called up for England in 1971 and was capped 19 times - winning those between 1971-1973.

Post-retirement, Storey turned his hand to being a pub landlord. He owned a pub called the Jolly Farmers, now renamed De Beauvoir Arms, which was situated just over a mile away from Highbury - Arsenal's former home.

However, as his own autobiography - True Storey: My Life and Crimes as a Football Hatchet Man - later details, Storey - who was married four times - was a 'confirmed ladies' man who loved a drink' and his establishment 'became a magnet for north London villains'.

Storey, who played at right back and in midfield, won 19 caps for England between 1971-1973

Post-retirement, Storey got on the wrong side of the law multiple times for various offences

Becoming acquaintances with criminals 'the Barry brothers' ended up seeing Storey serve time in prison as a result.

Storey aided the siblings' counterfeit operation by providing the finance and storage of the cast die for them to do so.

The trio were eventually caught and arrested - with Storey serving three years in prison at Wandsworth and Spring Hill for his actions.

However, the story does not end there. Far from it.

While on bail for conspiracy to produce counterfeit money, Storey looked to raise quick capital to flee to Spain.

Storey sought to do so by starting a brothel.

Called the Calypso Massage Parlour, he set it up with three associates. That operation was short-lived though as he was arrested in December 1979, handed a £700 fine and given a six-month suspended sentence.

There were other run-ins with the law too. He was also briefly jailed for contempt of court after failing to appear at his bankruptcy hearings.

After his run-ins with the law, Storey moved to the south of France later in life (pictured in 2010)

In April 1982, he was given a 12-month suspended sentence for stealing two cars he had on hire purchase whilst running his minicab firm.

Eight years later, he spent 28 days in jail for attempting to import porn videos from Europe. However, he was caught when the videos were found in a spare tyre smuggled into the UK.

Storey, who later in life moved to the south of France, sold the majority of memorabilia for £20,000 years ago. However, he leaves behind plenty of memories as a player and post-retirement.

#1555. Liverpool Open Talks With Argentine Midfielder: Is He Worth A New Deal?

Liverpool transfer news: Liverpool have opened contract talks with Alexis Mac Allister, according to @tribuna_ftbl, with his current deal running until June 2028. The report arrives days after his father, Carlos, told ESPN that no discussions had started, although he hinted at news before the end of the year.

It also reverses the summer, when the club extended Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai but made no offer to the 27-year-old, something Mac Allister revealed in September while admitting he had stayed despite chances to leave.

His form explains the change. After a poor 2025/26 under Arne Slot, he has become Andoni Iraola’s first-choice midfielder alongside Szoboszlai, pushing Gravenberch to the bench. He has scored once in the Premier League and three times in the Champions League, including the winner against Atlético Madrid, and holds a 7.29 FotMob average rating across 758 league minutes. Liverpool sit fourth.

FotMob places him in the 88th percentile among midfielders for shot attempts, and he has said the man-to-man system suits him because it demands less communication than Slot’s approach. His weaknesses are just as clear.

His defensive contributions (45th percentile) and aerial duels (46th) sit below the midfield average, and pundit David Lynch has questioned whether his legs have gone in Iraola’s 4-4-2, where two central midfielders cover huge areas. He has also collected four league yellow cards already.

Yes, but not on the terms his summer rebound might demand. Ten league games of good form do not cancel a season in which he looked off the pace, so Liverpool should offer around three years, with wages pitched below the bumper deals Gravenberch and Szoboszlai signed.

The timing still makes sense. With 18 months left, he enters the final year next summer, when Liverpool would face either a discounted sale or a free departure. His FotMob valuation of €66m has almost halved from the €130m peak of September 2025, so selling now would lock in the lowest price.

Iraola also needs a controller to sit beside Szoboszlai’s runs, and no one in the squad does that better. The caveat is that Mac Allister turns 28 next month, so Liverpool must pair him with a quicker partner next summer rather than treat his renewal as the end of the midfield rebuild.

#1554. Real Madrid: Mourinho faces attacking dilemma ahead of Champions League clash with PSV

By Axel Clody | 23 Nov 2026 13:19

Real Madrid go into Tuesday's Champions League clash with PSV on the back of nine consecutive victories, but with important issues for Jose Mourinho to manage. Saturday's 2-1 comeback win over Celta Vigo was another example of the team's ability to react, but it also exposed problems that the manager cannot ignore.

Vinicius Junior came off the bench to take a direct part in both goals, with the assist for Carlos Espi deciding the match. The Brazilian, who had served a four-match suspension in La Liga, has regained prominence and has already had his place in the starting line-up for the European tie confirmed by Mourinho. At the same time, the Spanish centre-forward again showed that he can be decisive even with few minutes on the pitch.

The challenge is to find room for so many options without compromising the collective structure. Real Madrid have Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius, Jude Bellingham, Arda Guler, Yan Diomande and Espi, as well as names who could come into the mix, such as Endrick and Bernardo Silva, but they cannot simply put them all on the pitch and hope that individual talent solves everything.

Vinicius's display against Celta was a reminder of what the Brazilian offers Real Madrid. Coming on 12 minutes into the second half, he gave the attack depth and was able to unbalance defenders in one-on-one situations. For the equaliser, he started the move that ended with Bellingham. For the winner, he crossed for Espi to pounce on the rebound.

Mourinho confirmed that the Brazilian will start against PSV, ending the debate about his status in the team. Peter Bosz's side are known for high pressing, aggressive defending and their attempts to win the ball back quickly. When that first press is beaten, however, they tend to offer space behind the defenders.

That is precisely where Vinicius can be decisive. With his acceleration and ability to attack the space in behind, the Brazilian is a constant threat to a defence that often plays a high line and takes on individual duels all over the pitch. Mbappe can also exploit these spaces.

The question for Mourinho is how to make this threat work without leaving the midfield exposed. Real Madrid cannot rely solely on winning the ball back and launching it to the forwards. They need players close by to connect transitions and sustain possession when necessary.

The presence of Bellingham and Guler between the lines could be important. The Englishman offers ball-carrying and arrivals into the box, while the Turkey international has the quality to find passes that speed up the attack. But the team needs a solid base behind them. Without that, the freedom of the attacking players could prove costly.

Espi's situation is another dilemma. The 21-year-old forward scored the winner against Celta and has three goals in only 44 minutes played in La Liga this season. It is impressive efficiency, but it does not necessarily mean that he should start.

Mourinho was clear in explaining the Spaniard's characteristics. Espi is a penalty-box centre-forward, strong in the air, able to play with his back to goal and to attack the spaces close to the six-yard box. He is not, however, a forward with great mobility to take part constantly in build-up play. The manager also said that the squad does not have the right characteristics to play a pure 4-4-2 with Mbappe and Espi together.

Mbappe likes to start from the left or occupy the space between the full-back and the centre-back, but he is not a traditional winger who tracks the opposition full-back back into his own half. Vinicius also needs freedom to receive the ball wide and accelerate. Putting Espi alongside the Frenchman would require the two wide players to tuck in more and help form a four-man midfield line.

There are alternatives, but all involve compromises. Bellingham could play deeper, for example. The problem is that Real Madrid would lose part of the Englishman's ability to arrive in the box and would need a midfielder with greater defensive responsibility to compensate. It would also be possible to use Espi in matches where the opposition sit deep and offer less space for the runs of Vinicius and Mbappe.

Against tired defences and crosses, Espi offers something different from the other forwards in the squad. His efficiency as a substitute should not be confused with an obligation to change the whole structure of the team.

The win over Celta also left a warning. After turning the scoreline around, Real Madrid finished the game with four forwards on the pitch, as well as Bellingham and Guler in midfield. Mourinho admitted that the team became unbalanced and that he would have liked an extra substitution to bring on Tchouameni and restore defensive protection.

Under Bosz, PSV rely on high pressing, dominating possession, constant movement and a defence that often takes on individual duels. The full-backs can advance into midfield and the forwards take part in the press. It is an aggressive model, capable of suffocating opponents, but one that also leaves space when the first line is beaten.

The impact of each at Real Madrid in 2026-27

Direct involvements = goals + assists. In the Champions League, Vinicius played four games without a goal or an assist; Espi scored one goal in four games, against Roma. Points gained assume that, without Espi's goals, the three games would have ended in draws. Data up to 21 November 2026.

Sources: FotMob (Opta data), AS and TheStatsAPI

Real Madrid have the tools to exploit these gaps. Vinicius and Mbappe can attack the space in behind, while Bellingham and Guler have the ability to receive between the lines and speed up the transition. The difficulty will be doing so without turning the game into a series of attacks and counter-attacks.

Real Madrid won their first four league-phase games in the Champions League and are second, with 12 points. The positive run brings calm, but it does not remove the need to improve the collective performance.

Mourinho already has an answer to one of the questions: Vinicius will start. He also knows what Espi can offer and why he does not intend simply to put him alongside Mbappe. The bigger challenge is to make Real Madrid take advantage of the quality of their attackers without losing control of midfield.

#1553. Arsenal transfer news on Germany winger: Is second choice enough?

Arsenal transfer news: Arsenal like Kevin Schade, but he isn’t the winger they want most. Football.London’s Tom Canton reports that the Brentford forward is on the shortlist for the left flank, with RB Leipzig’s Antonio Nusa ranked above him. Canton says the 24-year-old Germany international is certainly appreciated at the Emirates.

The ranking reflects an awkward summer for Mikel Arteta. Arsenal sold Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli, missed out on Vinicius Junior and signed only Christos Tzolis for about £34m.

Tzolis started the first five league games, then suffered a hamstring injury on international duty. Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke have covered since, and Madueke rescued a point in Saturday’s 2-2 draw at Newcastle, which left Arsenal six points clear for now.

Nusa, the 21-year-old Norwegian winger, has six goals and eight assists in 15 matches for Leipzig. Sky Sports reports that the Bundesliga club won’t sell him in January, so a summer deal looks more realistic, with Leipzig reportedly valuing him between £60m and £77m. Schade is the quicker route, but Arsenal asked about him in the summer and got nowhere, according to TEAMtalk. His contract runs until 2028.

Schade has scored three times in ten Premier League appearances from 2.44 expected goals, and his pace suits a side that already creates through Tzolis. He can play either flank or centrally. The weaknesses show elsewhere: no assists, three chances created in 781 minutes, seven completed dribbles at a 25% success rate and 43.8% of duels won. FotMob values him at about £47m.

Not in January, and certainly not as a consolation. Arsenal lead the league, Tzolis remains the first-choice left winger, and Madueke has just shown he can deliver there. Schade would add depth, but he wouldn’t add what Arteta lacks: a winger who beats his man and drags two defenders with him against low blocks.

Nusa builds his game on exactly that, and his output at Leipzig now justifies waiting until next summer. Schade’s returns suggest he would sit behind a fit Tzolis, which is hard to justify at a price Brentford would set after already refusing an approach.

A bid becomes sensible only if Tzolis breaks down again or Leipzig block Nusa completely, because Schade needs no time to adapt to the Premier League. Even then, anything above £50m would pay for potential rather than production, and a 25% dribble success rate tells Arsenal he isn’t the specialist they need.

#1552. Ramos ‘happy’ to be back on target for Milan: “We are building something beautiful”

Goncalo Ramos got back on the scoresheet in AC Milan’s big win against Frosinone on Sunday evening, expressing his delight after the game.

The pressure has certainly been mounting on Ramos in the last few months. The high price tag paid in the summer came with certain expectations from the Milan fans and with just three goals to his name prior to today’s game, it’s easy to see why there was criticism.

As such, the Rossoneri will be hoping that the goal scored against Frosinone can be a turning point for the No.9. It wasn’t just that he scored the goal either; he got stuck in and played a part in the other goals as well, which we highlighted in the player ratings.

Speaking to Sky and DAZN after the game, as transcribed by MilanNews, Ramos shared his thoughts on the goal and also said that Milan are ‘building something beautiful’.

“I’m really happy to have scored. The most important thing is that we won and we played a good team game. The three points are always the most important thing.”

“Yes, everything is going very well here: the team, the spirit, the atmosphere. We’re getting to know each other better every day, every week, after every training session, and I think everyone can see it on the pitch like today.

“We’re building something beautiful, and we want to keep working and keep moving forward.”

#1551. Alonso ready to sell £47m Chelsea signing for a Barca star

Chelsea transfer news: Xabi Alonso wants Barcelona right-back Jules Koundé at Chelsea and is ready to sell Marco Palestra, his £47m summer signing, to make room, according to El Nacional. The outlet says Alonso has pushed the case, a claim it credits to FourFourTwo, and that Palestra has Serie A interest from Juventus, AC Milan and Napoli, though it mentions no bid.

Barcelona would reportedly listen to offers of around €50m, roughly £43m, because Hansi Flick doesn’t treat Koundé as untouchable. The 28-year-old has started three of six LaLiga games this season after an ankle sprain on 17 October kept him out for over a month. El Nacional calls him a backup behind Eric García and says he’d welcome the move.

Koundé completes 93.9% of his passes, wins 58.8% of his duels and has 58 France caps, a composed defender who could play right-back or on the right of a back three. His body is the worry: a hamstring problem in March, then an ankle injury that lingered.

Palestra won Serie A’s Defender of the Year award at Cagliari, and his 81 completed dribbles topped every defender in Europe’s top five leagues. A thigh injury delayed his Chelsea debut until October, and El Nacional puts him at 202 minutes across six matches. Alonso prefers Josh Acheampong at right-back and, per BBC Sport, uses Palestra from the bench before Malo Gusto. He scored once in 37 league games, and his crossing remains modest.

Not as a swap. Palestra is a wing-back who beats opponents on the outside, while Koundé is a passer and cover defender best placed on the right of three centre-backs. Selling one doesn’t remove the need for the other, and Chelsea’s real shortage is right-sided cover: Reece James is injured and has been used in midfield, and Acheampong, a centre-back by trade, is filling in at right-back.

Koundé would solve that, but Gusto is the sale to make. He has lost his place, is reportedly open to a January exit, and Chelsea priced him at £75m in June, so even a discounted fee would cover much of Koundé’s £43m.

Selling Palestra after 202 minutes would mean writing off a player Alonso recruited and said needs time to adapt, to buy a 28-year-old with a muscle-injury record. Chelsea were fifth, 11 points behind Arsenal, before Leeds visited, without European football. Buy Koundé if the medical is clean, sell Gusto and keep Palestra.
